**Trigger and consequence:** selected when the active `AROS` Workbench target builds `workbench-tools` (`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25`; `workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:28-34`) and its scan finds a readable partition table, then container construction performs its second open. The first wrapper and backend table contents become unreachable and leak; only the second table is closed during the container's scan. Repeated scans can accumulate leaked table wrappers and partition records, and operations that expected the original opened table to remain current instead use the replacement state. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart` (`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25`; `workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:28-34`). **Confidence:** high for the overwrite and unpaired first state on the selected caller sequence. Close the scan's table before constructing the container, or have the constructor consume the already-open state instead of reopening it. No QuickPart scan, disk, GUI operation, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#partition-table-wrapper-and-quickpart-repeated-open-caller-pass-ek9342-added-2026-10-22).

<a id="ek9343"></a>
### EK9343 — Withdrawn as a duplicate of DISK-078.

The source path is real: `AddFS()` allocates a `FileSysEntry`, calls `LoadFileSystem()`, and returns `IoErr()` on a NULL segment list without freeing the allocation (`rom/partition/fsloader.c:56-107`). The same source, trigger, and consequence are already documented as [DISK-078](AROS-disk.md#disk-078). Do not count EK9343 as a separate Exec/Kernel finding. The selected immediate and deferred `AddBootFileSystem()` paths both reach `AddFS()`; those callers do not establish a distinct defect.

<a id="ek9344"></a>
### EK9344 — DOSBoot's m68k mouse-menu and PAL/NTSC paths are compiled out by a mismatched macro.

Both m68k-specific blocks in `rom/dosboot/menu.c` use `#ifdef mc68000`: `buttonsPressed()`'s CIA/POT two-button probe (`:889-904`) and `toggleMode()`'s CIA resource, display-flag update and BEAMCON0 write (`:555-564`). The selected AROS m68k sources use the `__mc68000`/`__mc68000__` target macro spelling, including this file's adjacent `#if !defined(__mc68000__)` guard (`menu.c:39`) and the m68k DOSBoot bootstrap paths (`rom/dosboot/bootstrap.c:44,269`). With the bare `mc68000` guard false, the mouse probe is absent from `bootmenu_Init()`'s menu-request path (`menu.c:964-970`), and `toggleMode()` is an empty function even though the main page advertises the PAL/NTSC key action (`:787-793`) and the key event calls it (`:610-615`).

**Trigger and consequence:** on the selected AROS m68k build, users relying on holding both mouse buttons cannot request the DOSBoot menu through that documented probe; on a compatible classic Amiga display, the advertised key action does not change PAL/NTSC mode. Keyboard menu requests remain available. **Affected configuration:** DOSBoot built for AROS m68k; the mouse/toggle hardware behavior specifically applies when `ciaa.resource` and the classic Amiga CIA/Paula display registers are present. **Confidence:** high that the guards exclude these blocks under the AROS m68k macro spelling; the menu-entry and display consequences follow from the selected callers. Use the project's `__mc68000` spelling for both guards. No menu, keyboard, mouse, display or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-menu-full-body-and-caller-reconciliation-ek9344-added-2026-10-22).

<a id="ek9345"></a>
### EK9345 — Concurrent synchronous `SystemTagList()` calls can restore a stale console break target.

For a synchronous launch with interactive input, `SystemTagList()` asks the input handler to change its break-signal task to the new CLI process's message-port task and saves the previous target in a local `oldSignal` (`rom/dos/systemtaglist.c:408,465-470`). After the child shell finishes and replies to the startup packet, the caller restores that saved target (`:485-486`; `compiler/include/dos/cliinit.h:180-193`). The selected console handler implements `ACTION_CHANGE_SIGNAL` as an unprotected read/replace of the single `fh->breaktask` field, returning the replaced pointer (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:1124-1132`). Incoming Ctrl-C signals that stored task (`rom/filesys/console_handler/support.c:1069-1071`). There is no per-filehandle stack or lock coordinating concurrent launchers.

If callers A and B use the same interactive FileHandle concurrently, A can save the original shell task and install A; B then saves A and installs B. If A's child finishes first, A restores the original task while B is still running. When B later finishes, B restores its saved A pointer, which may already refer to an exited child. Ctrl-C during B's run can therefore be delivered to the wrong task, and later console input can signal a stale task pointer. `SYS_Asynch=TRUE` skips the signal-target migration, so it does not take this path.

**Trigger and consequence:** two independent synchronous `SystemTagList()` callers overlap while sharing the same interactive console FileHandle, and their child shells complete out of order. The stored break target can be wrong during a child run and left pointing at an exited child afterward. **Affected configuration:** DOS builds using the selected console handler and synchronous launches with shared interactive input; the failure requires the stated concurrent shared-handle use. The checked-in direct caller census did not establish an in-tree overlapping same-handle sequence, so this remains a conditional API-level candidate. **Confidence:** high for the unsynchronized single-slot overwrite/restore behavior; occurrence depends on concurrent callers sharing the handle and out-of-order completion. Serialize ownership changes per handle or use a nesting-safe ownership mechanism. No launch, signal, or interleaving was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#console-break-target-systemtaglist-overlap-pass-ek9345).

<a id="ek9346"></a>
### EK9346 — BCMGENET RX reuses buffers without post-DMA cache invalidation on ARM32.

The BCMGENET receive path calls `CachePostDMA(buf, ...)` after the device has filled a slot, then reads the packet and returns the slot to the ring; the same cached buffer is reused without another `CachePreDMA()` (`workbench/devs/networks/bcmgenet/bcmgenet_unit.c:934-995`). The ARM-native Exec manifest selects `cachepredma` but no `cachepostdma` override (`arch/arm-native/exec/mmakefile.src:27-32`), so the generic `rom/exec/cachepostdma.c:44-49` no-op is used. The receive buffers are cacheable `MEMF_PUBLIC` allocations; their 64-byte alignment and 1,536-byte stride avoid sharing cache lines with adjacent slots, but do not invalidate stale lines within a reused slot (`bcmgenet_unit.c:222-237`). AArch64 Raspberry Pi has a real `CachePostDMA()` override and is not covered by this finding.

If the BCM2711 GENET DMA path is noncoherent, after the CPU has cached a slot's previous packet, a later device write to that slot can leave the cache stale; the subsequent receive callback can consume bytes from the previous frame rather than the new one. The source review did not establish whether the hardware path is noncoherent, so this data-corruption consequence is conditional on that platform property.

**Trigger and consequence:** an explicit 32-bit Raspberry Pi BCMGENET build receives successive frames through a reused slot while DMA is noncoherent; the no-op post-DMA hook can leave the CPU reading stale packet contents. **Affected configuration:** 32-bit ARM Raspberry Pi builds that explicitly include `workbench-devs-networks-bcmgenet`; AArch64's selected override is excluded. **Confidence:** high that the ARM32 hook is a no-op and the slot is reused without another pre-DMA operation; medium/conditional that this causes stale reads on the relevant GENET hardware because DMA coherency is not established by the checked-in source. Invalidate the received slot after DMA or allocate it from memory with a verified coherent/uncached mapping. No DMA, cache operation, packet, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#arm32-bcmgenet-rx-cachepostdma-reuse-pass-ek9346).

<a id="ek9347"></a>
### EK9347 — QuickPart never closes the root partition handle it opens for a scanned disk.

`QPDisk__MUIM_QPart_Disk_ScanForParts()` stores the result of `OpenRootPartition()` in `data->qpd_Disk_PH` and passes that handle into the partition-container object (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccDisk.c:204-206,269-273`). The selected container uses it to open and close partition-table state, but its `OM_DISPOSE` method only delegates to the superclass and does not close the root (`QP_ccPartitionContainer.c:771-781`). The owning disk object's `OM_DISPOSE` deletes its IO request and message port, then delegates; it does not call `CloseRootPartition()` (`QP_ccDisk.c:593-609`). The QuickPart source contains no `CloseRootPartition()` call. The partition library's root close path is responsible for closing the device and freeing the root handle (`rom/partition/closerootpartition.c:47-71`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the QuickPart target selected by the active `AROS` Workbench tools aggregate scans a disk successfully enough for `OpenRootPartition()` to return a handle, then the disk/container objects are disposed or another scan replaces them. The root handle and its partition-library/device resources remain allocated/open. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`. **Confidence:** high for the missing close across both object disposal paths; each successful root open is leaked. Close the root handle from its owning disk object's disposal after dependent table/container state has been closed. No disk scan, object disposal, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-disk-root-handle-lifecycle-pass-ek9347).

<a id="ek9348"></a>
### EK9348 — QuickPart leaves its disk device open when disposing a disk object.

`QPDisk__OM_NEW()` creates an IO request and successfully calls `OpenDevice()` before building the MUI object (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccDisk.c:395-403`). That open is not closed on the success path. The later scan calls `OpenDevice()` again using the same IO request and calls `CloseDevice()` once after its identify probe (`QP_ccDisk.c:183-202`), balancing only the scan's open. `QPDisk__OM_DISPOSE()` deletes the IO request and message port without closing the constructor's remaining device reference (`QP_ccDisk.c:593-609`). Exec's `OpenDevice()` clears and reuses the request's device field on each open, while `CloseDevice()` releases one open and marks the request closed; deleting the request does not perform the missing close (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:99-123`; `rom/exec/closedevice.c:46-83`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the QuickPart target selected by the active `AROS` Workbench tools aggregate successfully constructs a disk object and later disposes it. Its construction-time device open remains outstanding, retaining the device open count/unit state; repeated object creation can retain additional opens. The scan's paired open/close does not release the constructor reference. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`. **Confidence:** high for the unmatched successful constructor open and missing close before request deletion. Close the initial device open during disposal, and close it on any constructor failure after the successful open. No device or GUI operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-disk-device-open-close-accounting-ek9348).

<a id="ek9349"></a>
### EK9349 — QuickPart dereferences a null IO request after port or request allocation failure.

`QPDisk__OM_NEW()` calls `CreateMsgPort()` and immediately passes its result to `CreateIORequest()` without checking either allocation (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccDisk.c:392-397`). Exec's `CreateIORequest()` returns NULL when its reply port is NULL or when its allocation fails (`rom/exec/createiorequest.c:63-75`). QuickPart then calls `OpenDevice()` unconditionally with that result (`QP_ccDisk.c:400`). Exec's selected `OpenDevice()` implementation immediately writes `io_Unit` through its request argument before checking whether a device was found (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:99-108`), so the null request dereference occurs before QuickPart can reject device-open failure or construct the object.

**Trigger and consequence:** QuickPart disk-object construction in a build selected by the active `AROS` Workbench tools aggregate experiences `CreateMsgPort()` failure, `CreateIORequest()` failure, or the port failure that causes `CreateIORequest()` to reject a NULL port. The subsequent `OpenDevice()` dereferences NULL and the task faults instead of returning a clean construction failure. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`. **Confidence:** high for both Exec allocation return contracts and the unchecked NULL passed into `OpenDevice()`. Check the port and request allocations before opening the device, and unwind any successful earlier allocation on failure. No allocation failure, device open, GUI operation, or build was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-io-request-allocation-failure-path-ek9349).

<a id="ek9350"></a>
### EK9350 — QuickPart writes through a failed disk-name allocation.

In `QPDisk__MUIM_QPart_Disk_ScanForParts()`, when the disk object already has a supplied name, the function allocates a replacement and immediately calls `strcpy()` without checking the allocation (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccDisk.c:187-192`). When there is no supplied name, it allocates the identification buffer and then unconditionally passes it to `QPDisk__Func_IdentifyDrive()`; successful ATA/SCSI identification writes through it in `QPDisk__Func_w2strcpy()`, while failed identification falls through to `sprintf()` into it (`QP_ccDisk.c:194-200,75-80,104-124`). Thus either disk-name allocation failure reaches a write through NULL. The separate verbose-name allocation is checked before use and is not part of this finding (`QP_ccDisk.c:241-248`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the QuickPart scan in a build selected by the active `AROS` Workbench tools aggregate opens its device successfully, then the replacement-name or identification-buffer allocation fails. The subsequent copy/identify/fallback write dereferences NULL and faults the scan task instead of continuing without a display name or returning a clean allocation error. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`. **Confidence:** high for both unchecked allocation branches and their NULL-writing consumers. Check each allocation before copying or identifying, and report/skip the disk on failure. No allocation failure, device, scan, GUI operation, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-disk-name-allocation-failure-pass-ek9350).

<a id="ek9351"></a>
### EK9351 — QuickPart's fixed-width disk-name trimmer can truncate the final word or walk before its buffer.

`QPDisk__Func_w2strcpy()` copies every input word, then moves the output pointer back by two `UWORD`s before trimming spaces/zeros (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccDisk.c:75-86`). This skips the final output word when deciding where the C string ends: if the penultimate word is padding but the final word contains a character, the loop zeros the penultimate word and terminates before the final character. More seriously, if all copied words are spaces or zero, the loop reaches a read before the beginning of the output buffer; if that adjacent byte is also zero or a space, it writes there and continues backward. The selected callers supply fixed 40-byte ATA model data and 16-byte SCSI product data (`QP_ccDisk.c:104-124`); the allocated output buffer is large enough for forward copying, but the backward trim has no lower-bound check (`:195-200`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the QuickPart scan in a build selected by the active `AROS` Workbench tools aggregate successfully receives an ATA/SCSI identify response whose fixed-width model/product field is all spaces or zero, causing an out-of-bounds read before the output buffer and, depending on the adjacent byte, a write there; a field with padding in the penultimate word and a nonblank final word is instead displayed truncated. These device-response patterns are conditional and were not established on a particular disk. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`. **Confidence:** high for the unbounded backward loop and skipped final word; occurrence depends on the returned fixed-width identify bytes. Trim from the actual end, preserve a terminating NUL, and stop at the buffer start. No identify response, scan, GUI operation, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-disk-identity-trimmer-bounds-pass-ek9351).

<a id="ek9352"></a>
### EK9352 — QuickPart reads the SCSI Inquiry product field from byte offset 32 instead of 16.

The SCSI Inquiry response is a byte stream. The checked-in `atapitest` reads the 8-byte vendor field at `buf + 8` and the 16-byte product field at `buf + 16`; the local `scsi_inquiry_data_t` likewise places `product[16]` after `vendor[8]` (`developer/debug/test/devices/ata/atapitest.c:202`; `developer/debug/devtest/devtest.c:158-160`). QuickPart stores the response in `UWORD data[]`, then passes `&data[16]` to a helper that copies 16 bytes (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccDisk.c:113-124`). Since each `UWORD` is two bytes, this starts at response byte 32, the revision/vendor-specific region, not the product field at byte 16 (which would be `&data[8]`). On a successful SCSI Inquiry fallback, QuickPart therefore displays unrelated response bytes as the product name.

**Trigger and consequence:** the QuickPart scan in a build selected by the active `AROS` Workbench tools aggregate's ATA Identify fails, and its SCSI Inquiry command succeeds with a normal response. The displayed name is sourced from bytes 32–47 rather than the 16-byte product field. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart` and devices/controllers that successfully service this SCSI Inquiry path; ATA Identify success bypasses it. **Confidence:** high for the byte-offset arithmetic and in-tree Inquiry layout; the successful fallback depends on the device/controller. Read the product from byte offset 16, with byte-oriented access. No Inquiry, device, or GUI operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-scsi-inquiry-product-offset-pass-ek9352).

<a id="ek9353"></a>
### EK9353 — QuickPart byte-swaps raw SCSI Inquiry product characters on little-endian targets.

QuickPart reuses `QPDisk__Func_w2strcpy()` for both ATA Identify and SCSI Inquiry. The helper applies `AROS_BE2WORD()` to every two-byte pair before storing it (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccDisk.c:75-86,123-124`). That conversion is appropriate for ATA Identify's word-encoded model field, but SCSI Inquiry product data is a byte string; the selected test caller prints `buf + 16` directly as a 16-byte string (`developer/debug/test/devices/ata/atapitest.c:202`). On little-endian AROS, `AROS_BE2WORD()` swaps each pair, so the two product characters in every word are reversed. This is independent of EK9352's offset: after correcting the offset, the wrong character order remains unless SCSI bytes bypass the ATA word conversion.

**Trigger and consequence:** a little-endian build of optional QuickPart reaches a successful SCSI Inquiry fallback and displays the product string. Adjacent characters are reversed in pairs, making the reported disk model garbled. **Affected configuration:** explicit QuickPart builds for little-endian targets and SCSI devices/controllers whose Inquiry fallback succeeds; big-endian targets are excluded, and ATA Identify uses the separate word-encoded path. **Confidence:** high for the conversion on little-endian targets and the byte-string response layout; occurrence depends on use of the SCSI fallback. Copy SCSI response bytes without word swapping. No Inquiry, device, or GUI operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-scsi-inquiry-endian-pass-ek9353).

<a id="ek9354"></a>
### EK9354 — QuickPart discards the trailing free extent when adding an interior partition.

When `QPPartitionContainer__MUIM_QPart_ccPartitionContainer_AddPart()` finds a new partition inside a free-space node, it first shortens that node's `PCCN_End` to `Part_Start - 1` if the partition starts at least one 512-byte block after the free-space start (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccPartitionContainer.c:245-264`). It then tests whether the partition ends at least one block before that already-shortened end (`:273-281`). For an ordinary interior partition, the test is now false, so the remaining free extent from `Part_End + 1` through the original free end is never created. `InsertPartEntry()` adds the partition and only adds a trailing free node when that test flag was set (`:78-90,148-164,171-190`).

For example, inserting `[3000,4999]` into a free extent `[1000,8999]` changes the existing free end to `2999`; the later tail check compares `4999` against the shortened end and fails. QuickPart's child model then contains the pre-partition free extent and new partition, but not `[5000,8999]`. The storage remains unpartitioned; the lost extent is in the editor's model/UI and is unavailable for subsequent partition placement in that session.

**Trigger and consequence:** QuickPart loads or adds a partition whose start and end are both interior to a represented free extent, with its start at least 512 bytes after that extent's start. The post-partition free range is omitted from the child list. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`. **Confidence:** high for the mutation-before-tail-check and omitted extent; it does not claim on-disk data loss. Save the original free end before shrinking the prefix and derive the trailing extent from that saved value. No disk, editor, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-partition-container-free-extent-recheck-ek9354).

<a id="ek9355"></a>
### EK9355 — QuickPart leaves a trailing free-space node spanning a later partition

QPPartitionContainer__MUIM_QPart_ccPartitionContainer_FindParts() scans each table partition in linked-list order and calls AddPart() (workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccPartitionContainer.c:428-451). The initial container has one free node covering its full extent (:663-679). If partition 1 starts at the container lower bound and ends before the upper bound, AddPart() marks that node for deletion and creates a trailing free node (:245-279; InsertPartEntry() at :146-187). When FindParts() then processes a later disjoint partition 2, the first child is partition 1 and does not match partition 2. The insertion at :330-335 is unconditional on a containing-node match, appends partition 2, and breaks before examining the trailing free node. That free node retains its original range, which still includes partition 2. UpdateWeights() applies each node's stored weight to its child object (:457-489), so the editor's free-space model and proportional layout continue to count partition 2's blocks as free. This is distinct from EK9354, where a matching free node is found but its end is mutated before trailing space is checked.

**Trigger and consequence:** the optional QuickPart tool scans a table whose first partition begins at the container start and whose later disjoint partition lies inside the trailing free extent created for partition 1. The second partition is represented, but the free node is not split and retains a range that includes it; the editor's free-space model and proportional layout are inconsistent. **Affected configuration:** explicit builds of optional workbench-tools-quickpart. **Confidence:** high for the source-level list transition and stale free extent; the stated ordering follows the table's linked-list enumeration. Continue searching until a containing free node is found and split only that node. No disk scan, editor, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-addpart-containing-free-node-search-pass-ek9355).

<a id="ek9356"></a>
### EK9356 — QuickPart leaks partition-container bookkeeping nodes.

The container allocates a separate `PartCont_ChildIntern` for its initial free-space child and for each inserted partition/free-space child, links each node into `qpcd_Part_Children`, and also stores its pointer in the MUI child's `MUIA_UserData` (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccPartitionContainer.c:112-160,176-187,663-679`). When an existing free-space node is consumed, `AddPart()` removes it from the list with `Remove()` but does not free the allocation (`:353-356`). The container's `OM_DISPOSE` only delegates to the superclass; it neither drains the bookkeeping list nor frees those separately allocated nodes (`:771-780`). MUI child-object disposal does not own these independent `AllocVec()` blocks.

**Trigger and consequence:** in an explicit QuickPart build, scan a disk with a partition table that consumes free-space nodes, then dispose the resulting container. Each removed node and every node still linked at container disposal remains allocated; repeated scans/disposals accumulate these leaks. The list removal makes consumed nodes unreachable from the container, while disposal leaves surviving nodes without a cleanup path. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`, selected by the active `AROS` Workbench tools aggregate (`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25`; `workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:28-34`). **Confidence:** high for both removal and disposal paths; this is distinct from the unchecked bookkeeping-node allocation findings EK9357–EK9358. Free removed nodes and drain/free remaining bookkeeping nodes during disposal, clearing child user-data as needed. No disk scan, GUI operation, or allocation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-partition-container-bookkeeping-node-lifecycle-recheck-ek9356).

<a id="ek9357"></a>
### EK9357 — QuickPart dereferences a failed partition-node allocation while adding a partition.

`InsertPartEntry()` initializes `newPartNode` to NULL and only populates it when `AllocVec()` succeeds (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccPartitionContainer.c:82-83,128-143`). If that allocation fails and `MUIM_Group_InitChange` succeeds, the function still evaluates `&newPartNode->PCCN_Node` in `AddTail()` (`:167-176`); it then calls `OM_ADDMEMBER` with the partition object and returns success.

**Trigger and consequence:** the optional QuickPart tool scans a disk partition and the bookkeeping-node allocation fails while the MUI group change begins. The null member access faults the scan task instead of reporting allocation failure; if execution gets past it, the code also proceeds as though insertion succeeded despite lacking a tracking node. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation and null dereference; occurrence depends on allocation failure and successful `MUIM_Group_InitChange`. Fail insertion and unwind any created child/spacer objects when the node allocation fails. No allocation, disk scan, GUI operation, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-partition-node-allocation-failure-recheck-ek9357).

<a id="ek9358"></a>
### EK9358 — QuickPart dereferences a failed initial free-space-node allocation.

During successful partition-container object construction, `contSpacerNode` is allocated for the initial full-extent free-space child, then immediately dereferenced to initialize its child, weight, type, bounds and list link without checking for NULL (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccPartitionContainer.c:663-679`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an explicit QuickPart build constructs a partition container and this bookkeeping allocation fails. The constructor writes through NULL and faults instead of returning a clean construction failure. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation and immediate dereference; occurrence depends on memory allocation failure on this constructor path. Check the allocation and unwind the already-created container child if it fails. No allocation, disk scan, GUI operation, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-initial-spacer-allocation-failure-recheck-ek9358).

<a id="ek9359"></a>
### EK9359 — QuickPart writes long DOS device names past a fixed stack buffer.

The partition-label builder declares `devNmBufTmp[64]`, obtains a DOS device-name BSTR and its length, copies at most 64 bytes with `strncpy()`, then writes `':'` at `devNmBufTmp[len]` and a terminator at `devNmBufTmp[len + 1]` (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccPartition.c:317-330`). There is no length check. BSTR names can be longer than 62 characters; at length 63 the terminator is already one byte out of bounds, and at lengths of 64 or more both writes extend beyond the array.

**Trigger and consequence:** an explicit QuickPart build scans a partition while the DOS device list contains an eligible filesystem device entry (`dol_Task` and startup message set) whose BSTR name is at least 63 characters. The label path writes beyond its stack buffer before the `IsFileSystem()` check, potentially corrupting adjacent stack data. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`. **Confidence:** high for the fixed extent and unchecked index; reachability depends on such a long eligible device name being present during the scan. Reject or safely truncate names that do not leave room for the colon and terminator. No DOS list or GUI operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-dos-device-name-stack-buffer-recheck-ek9359).

<a id="ek9360"></a>
### EK9360 — QuickPart displays each partition one sector smaller than its inclusive extent.

The displayed-size calculation counts cylinders, surfaces and blocks per track to obtain the inclusive block count, subtracts one, then multiplies by sector size (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccPartition.c:293-300`). For an extent of N sectors, the inclusive count is N, so this produces `(N - 1) * sectorSize` bytes: one sector below the actual size. The partition's separate start/end attribute calculations retain their inclusive endpoints (`:439-452`); this finding concerns the displayed size string.

**Trigger and consequence:** a QuickPart partition object displays its size label; for every nonempty extent, the value is under-reported by one sector before unit scaling/formatting. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`. **Confidence:** high for the arithmetic and its scope to display formatting. Multiply the inclusive sector count by sector size without subtracting one. No disk scan or GUI operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-inclusive-partition-size-display-recheck-ek9360).

<a id="ek9361"></a>
### EK9361 — QuickPart passes a failed size-string allocation to `%s`.

The partition constructor stores `StrDup(partLabelTxt)` in `data->qppd_Str_Size` and immediately uses that pointer as the second `%s` argument to `sprintf()` without checking for NULL (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccPartition.c:300-303`). The resulting label is then passed to MUI (`:304-305`).

**Trigger and consequence:** QuickPart constructs a partition label and the `StrDup()` allocation for the formatted size fails. The NULL pointer is consumed as a C string by `sprintf()`; the resulting behavior is implementation-dependent and may fault or produce an invalid label, rather than reporting a clean allocation failure. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked NULL flow; the exact manifestation depends on the selected C library's `%s` handling for NULL. Check the allocation and unwind or omit the label on failure. No allocation or GUI operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-size-string-allocation-failure-recheck-ek9361).

<a id="ek9362"></a>
### EK9362 — QuickPart does not release its duplicated partition strings.

The partition constructor stores heap strings returned by `StrDup()` in `qppd_Str_Type`, `qppd_Str_Size`, `qppd_Str_Label` and, when a matching mounted DOS device is found, `qppd_Str_DOSDev` (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccPartition.c:243,301-303,349`). The partition object's `OM_DISPOSE` method only delegates to its superclass and does not release these duplicates (`:463-472`). In the container-partition branch, `qppd_Str_Label` aliases `qppd_Str_Type` (`:270`), so that alias must not be freed twice.

**Trigger and consequence:** an explicit QuickPart build creates and later disposes partition objects. Each independently duplicated string remains allocated; repeatedly opening/closing or replacing partition views accumulates these leaks. The alias assignment does not create an additional allocation. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`. **Confidence:** high for the allocations and absence of frees in the disposal method; leak size/count depends on which constructor branches run. Release each distinct owned string once during disposal. No GUI or allocation operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-partition-string-ownership-recheck-ek9362).

<a id="ek9363"></a>
### EK9363 — QuickPart passes a failed graphics-region allocation to `OrRectRegion()`.

When the partition is the active QuickPart part, `QPPartition__MUIM_Draw()` calls `NewRegion()` and unconditionally passes its result to `OrRectRegion()` before checking `r` (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccPartition.c:520,527-565`). `NewRegion()` may return NULL on allocation failure. The selected Graphics implementation dereferences the region argument (`rom/graphics/orrectregion.c:75-86`), so the later `if (r)` guard around `MUI_AddClipRegion()` cannot protect this call.

**Trigger and consequence:** an explicit QuickPart build draws the active partition and region allocation fails. `OrRectRegion(NULL, ...)` dereferences NULL and faults the GUI task instead of skipping the clip region or handling allocation failure. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked result and selected callee dereference; occurrence depends on `NewRegion()` allocation failure. Check `r` before calling `OrRectRegion()` and continue drawing without the optional clip region when allocation fails. No allocation, graphics operation, GUI operation, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-region-allocation-failure-recheck-ek9363).

<a id="ek9364"></a>
### EK9364 — QuickPart's Apply and Undo controls do not apply or undo staged partition operations.

The main window creates an Apply button and an anonymous Undo button, but installs no notification for either; the only Apply notification is commented out (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_Main.c:522-524,655-662`). The Delete button is wired to `QPApp__MUIM_QPart_ccApp_DeleteActive()`, which adds a delete-operation object to the pending group and changes the in-memory view (`QP_ccApp.c:394-450`). The disk class's `MUIM_QPart_Disk_SaveDisk` method is an unconditional stub returning zero (`QP_ccDisk.c:627-628`); no selected Apply/Undo handler or disk write path is present in the reviewed caller set.

**Trigger and consequence:** in the explicit QuickPart application, delete a displayed partition and then press Apply or Undo. The controls have no action wiring, so the pending operation is neither committed to disk nor rolled back through those controls; the UI can display the staged delete while the backing table remains unchanged. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`. **Confidence:** high for the absent selected notifications, the wired delete staging path and the SaveDisk stub; this describes the checked-in QuickPart control flow, not unreviewed external extension behavior. Wire Apply to validate and commit staged operations and Undo to restore the staged model, or remove/disable the controls until implemented. No GUI or disk operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-apply-undo-control-caller-recheck-ek9364).

<a id="ek9365"></a>
### EK9365 — QuickPart appends `unknown>` after displayed GPT partition UUIDs.

In the active-partition details formatter, `QPApp__OM_SET()` handles a 16-byte partition type by calling `UUID_Unparse()` and updating `stroff`, but then falls through into the `default` case, which appends `unknown>` (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccApp.c:310-324`). The selected GPT backend sets `PartitionType.id_len` to `sizeof(uuid_t)` (16) (`rom/partition/partitiongpt.c:598-603`); `UUID_Unparse()` writes a canonical UUID string and terminator (`workbench/libs/uuid/uuid_parse.c:109-130`).

**Trigger and consequence:** select any GPT partition in explicit QuickPart. Its details display the correct type UUID followed by the misleading `unknown>` suffix. This is a presentation error; the reviewed code does not use the suffix to interpret or write the partition type. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`. **Confidence:** high for the 16-byte GPT path and switch fallthrough. Add a `break` after the UUID case. No GUI or disk operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-gpt-uuid-description-fallthrough-recheck-ek9365).

<a id="ek9366"></a>
### EK9366 — QuickPart omits the “primary” label for ordinary MBR partitions.

The active-partition formatter initializes `ContainerSubStr` to the non-NULL empty string. For an MBR parent it attempts to set the ordinary-partition label only when `!ContainerSubStr`, so that branch is never true; the preceding type switch changes the string only for extended/container identifiers 5, 15 and 48 (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccApp.c:241,255-288`). The final details formatter therefore prints `MBR partition` for ordinary primary entries, while the extended types receive their specific label.

**Trigger and consequence:** select an ordinary MBR primary partition in explicit QuickPart. Its details panel omits the “primary” classification; the partition type and table handling are not changed. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`. **Confidence:** high for the non-NULL empty-string initialization and conditional. Test the string contents or initialize it to NULL before assigning the ordinary label. No GUI or disk operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-mbr-primary-label-condition-recheck-ek9366).

<a id="ek9367"></a>
### EK9367 — QuickPart leaks a delete-operation object when free-space allocation fails.

The selected Delete handler creates `newOperObj` first, then allocates a `PartCont_ChildIntern` for the replacement free-space region (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccApp.c:416-423`). If that allocation fails, the `else` branch is empty; the operation object is neither added to the pending group nor disposed (`:451-460`). The handler has already cleared the app's active-part pointer (`:408-409`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an explicit QuickPart build deletes an active displayed partition and the replacement free-space bookkeeping allocation fails after operation-object construction. The unattached MUI operation object and its resources leak, and QuickPart has already cleared its active selection without staging the delete. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`. **Confidence:** high for the allocation ordering and empty failure branch; occurrence depends on the allocation failure. Dispose the operation object and restore/retain active state when replacement allocation fails. No allocation or GUI operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-delete-operation-allocation-failure-recheck-ek9367).

<a id="ek9368"></a>
### EK9368 — QuickPart divides by zero while scaling discovered disks with no nonzero capacity.

`qpED.qped_DriveLargest` is initialized to zero. During storage enumeration, each drive record is retained even when `OpenRootPartition()` fails; in that case its zero-initialized size is unchanged. Successful probes can also leave size zero when the reported geometry product is zero (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_FindDisks.c:75,107-134,211-213`). Later, for every listed drive, `QP_FindDisks()` unconditionally computes `(newDrive->qpfd_Size * 100) / qpED.qped_DriveLargest` (`:231-252`).

**Trigger and consequence:** QuickPart discovers at least one eligible storage unit, but every root-partition probe fails or every reported capacity is zero. The largest-capacity denominator remains zero and disk-list construction reaches integer division by zero, faulting the GUI task. If no drives are listed, the loop is skipped and this division does not occur. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`. **Confidence:** high for the initialized/conditional maximum and unconditional division; trigger requires a nonempty list with no nonzero size. Skip scaling when the maximum is zero or reject zero-capacity records. No storage enumeration or GUI operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-zero-largest-capacity-scaling-recheck-ek9368).

<a id="ek9369"></a>
### EK9369 — QuickPart calls `UUID_Unparse()` after `uuid.library` fails to open.

`main()` stores the result of `OpenLibrary("uuid.library", 0)` in the global `UUIDBase` but does not check it before continuing into GUI/class initialization (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_Main.c:314,348-358`). The GPT active-partition details path later calls `UUID_Unparse()` for 16-byte IDs (`QP_ccApp.c:318-320`); the selected UUID vector implementation uses `UUIDBase` as its library base.

**Trigger and consequence:** in an explicit QuickPart build, `uuid.library` is unavailable or fails to open, and the user selects a GPT partition. QuickPart reaches the UUID vector with a NULL library base, so the details update cannot safely dispatch and may fault. Non-GPT partitions do not take this call path. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart` with GPT partition support. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked open and conditional GPT call; manifestation depends on library-vector dispatch with a null base. Abort initialization if the required library is unavailable. No library failure, GUI operation, or disk operation was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-uuid-library-open-failure-recheck-ek9369).

<a id="ek9370"></a>
### EK9370 — QuickPart leaves custom classes, the UUID library reference and storage attribute base unreleased.

On startup, QuickPart opens `uuid.library`, obtains the HIDD storage-unit attribute base, and creates up to eight MUI custom classes (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_Main.c:350,358-369,194-201`). After the application object is disposed, the exit path closes MUIMaster and Expansion but never calls `MUI_DeleteCustomClass()`, `OOP_ReleaseAttrBases(storage_abd)` or `CloseLibrary(UUIDBase)` (`:720-733`). The chained class-creation expression can also fail partway through, reaching the same cleanup without deleting classes already created. MUI documents `MUI_DeleteCustomClass()` for releasing classes from `MUI_CreateCustomClass()`; OOP's obtain/release routines pair attribute-base references (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_deletecustomclass.c:20-41`; `rom/oop/obtainattrbases.c:20-71`; `rom/oop/releaseattrbases.c:19-62`).

**Trigger and consequence:** run the explicit QuickPart program to normal exit, or encounter a later custom-class creation failure after earlier classes were created. The opened UUID library reference, obtained storage attribute base, and created class resources are not released; repeated invocations or partial initialization failures accumulate resources. **Affected configuration:** builds where the active `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`. **Confidence:** high for the missing cleanup calls and API ownership pairing; exact retained resources depend on how far initialization succeeds. Delete each non-NULL created class after disposing application objects, release the acquired attribute base, and close UUIDBase on all exits. No program run or initialization failure was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#quickpart-startup-resource-release-recheck-ek9370).

<a id="ek9371"></a>
### EK9371 — RISC-V CPU alerts treat saved `s0` as a frame chain despite frame-pointer omission.

For a user-mode CPU trap, `Exec_TrapHandler()` publishes the saved `ctx->FP` as `iet_AlertStack` and copies the CPU context for later alert formatting (`rom/exec/traphandler.c:100-112`). On RISC-V, `ctx->FP` is saved register x8/s0. The selected RISC-V `UnwindFrame()` assumes that value is a CFA and unconditionally reads `frame[-1]` and `frame[-2]` (`arch/riscv64-all/exec/alert_cpu.c:40-49`). `FormatAlertExtra()` checks only `TypeOfMem(fp)` before calling it (`rom/exec/alertextra.c:149-168`), which does not verify that the address contains a frame record. The selected RISC-V backtrace source explicitly states that the target is built with `-fomit-frame-pointer` and has no frame chain (`arch/riscv64-all/kernel/backtracefromframe.c:15-22`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a RISC-V CPU alert enters the user-level alert formatter. The saved s0 is interpreted as a frame-chain address even though normal selected code does not maintain that chain; the resulting trace can be invalid. If s0 is a `TypeOfMem()`-accepted address near an allocation boundary, the two preceding-word reads can cross that allocation and may fault if the adjacent memory is inaccessible. The RI debugger's separate context formatter does not take this alert-unwind path. **Affected configuration:** RISC-V CPU alerts using the selected RISC-V alert formatter; the frame-chain assumption applies to the selected RV64 kernel build and the shared RISC-V alert helper. **Confidence:** high that the trace model conflicts with the selected compiler mode; an out-of-allocation read or secondary fault additionally depends on the saved s0 value. Use the target's stack-scan backtrace approach or validate an actual frame-record contract before walking. No trap, alert or debug operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#risc-v-alert-frame-chain-recheck-ek9371).

<a id="ek9372"></a>
### EK9372 — Hosted emergency-console startup leaks DOS resources on failure paths.

The selected hosted emergency-console resident opens `dos.library` before acquiring the `emul-handler` resource and the `EMU` device process (`arch/all-hosted/filesys/emul_handler/boot.c:70,137-143`). If either acquisition fails, it returns without closing the DOS library. It then allocates the stdin and stdout DOS FileHandles; if stdout allocation fails, it closes DOS but does not `FreeDosObject()` the already allocated stdin handle (`:145-157`; the paired release routine frees DOS_FILEHANDLE allocations at `rom/dos/freedosobject.c:55-61`). After installing both handles as the process input/output and console-error stream, a failed synchronous `SystemTags()` call prints an error and calls `RemTask(NULL)` without closing either handle (`boot.c:159-190`). With no stream tags, the selected `SystemTagList()` inherits `Input()` and `Output()` and leaves their `*_opened` flags false, so its failure cleanup does not close these caller-owned handles (`rom/dos/systemtaglist.c:101-113,133-135,505-509`). Exec task removal does not perform DOS `Close()`/`FreeDosObject()` cleanup for those allocations (`rom/exec/remtask.c:115-141`).

**Trigger and consequence:** on a hosted target with the emergency-console resident enabled, display startup fails and one of these later boot steps fails: opening the handler resource, finding `EMU`, allocating stdout after stdin succeeded, or creating the synchronous emergency shell. The corresponding DOS library reference or independently allocated FileHandle remains unreleased; the first two branches retain the library open, the stdout-allocation branch leaks stdin, and shell-creation failure leaves both installed handles unclosed before task removal. The initial stdin-allocation failure does close DOS and is not part of this finding. **Affected configuration:** non-mobile hosted targets whose emul-handler manifest includes `boot`; configured mobile variants define `NO_EMERGENCY_CONSOLE` and exclude this path (`arch/all-hosted/filesys/emul_handler/emul.conf:14`; `mmakefile.src:20`). **Confidence:** high for the explicit ownership and missing cleanup branches; occurrence requires the stated startup failure. Close the library and free any allocated DOS objects on each early return, and close the installed handles before removing the process. No hosted boot or failure was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#hosted-emergency-console-failure-cleanup-recheck-ek9372).

<a id="ek9373"></a>
### EK9373 — Sam440 `Disable()` can permanently drop 50 Hz timer-device ticks.

The Sam440 `SC_CLI` syscall masks the UIC external-interrupt enable register, while `SC_STI` restores the selected external-interrupt mask (`arch/ppc-sam440/kernel/syscall.c:69-77`). The platform separately configures the PowerPC decrementer as an auto-reloading 50 Hz interrupt (`kernel_startup.c:566-572`). That decrementer is not masked by the UIC operation, so it continues firing during `Disable()`. In `decrementer_handler()`, the VBlank cause is issued only when `SysBase->IDNestCnt < 0` (`arch/ppc-sam440/kernel/intr.c:299-337`); when disabled, each tick is acknowledged but no VBlank event is raised. The selected Exec `Enable()` decrements the nesting count, reenables interrupts and handles pending soft interrupts/rescheduling, but does not replay missed VBlank events (`rom/exec/enable.c:83-125`).

**Trigger and consequence:** on Sam440, a `Disable()` interval spans one or more 50 Hz decrementer events. Those events are not queued for later VBlank processing, so timer.device/VBlank consumers receive fewer ticks than elapsed decrementer periods; re-enabling does not catch up. **Affected configuration:** PPC-Sam440 builds using this kernel decrementer/VBlank path. **Confidence:** high for the UIC-only masking, auto-reload source and `IDNestCnt` gate; the number of lost events depends on the duration and phase of the disabled interval. Use a pending-tick count or another mechanism that preserves elapsed VBlank events across Disable/Enable. No interrupt or timer operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#sam440-disable-decrementer-vblank-recheck-ek9373).

<a id="ek9374"></a>
### EK9374 — SAD's task-list command traverses mutable SMP lists without their read locks.

The `ST` command in `InternalDebug()` walks `TaskRunning` with `ForeachNode()` and walks `TaskReady` and `TaskWait` with `GetHead()`/`GetSucc()`, but acquires none of the corresponding task-list read locks (`rom/exec/debug_internal.c:233-259`). The selected PC ExecSMP scheduler and `RemTask()` mutate these lists under per-list spinlocks; task removal can unlink the node and free the task's `tc_MemEntry` chain (`rom/exec/exec_intern.h:193-227`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:91-112,160-181`). The ordinary SAD entry path does not stop other processors: `Debug()` reaches `InternalDebug()`, and PC `KrnObtainInput()` returns without a global scheduler stop (`arch/all-pc/kernel/obtaininput.c:14-23`; coverage trace at [L3623](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L3623)).

**Trigger and consequence:** on selected PC ExecSMP, run SAD's `ST` command while other CPUs schedule or remove tasks. The traversal can follow a list link while its node is being moved or removed, print inconsistent task data, or dereference a task node after it has been freed. **Affected configuration:** x86/x86-64 PC targets built with ExecSMP and the SAD/debug command enabled. **Confidence:** high for the missing locks and concurrent writer synchronization; an actual invalid traversal depends on overlap timing. Take matching list read locks while traversing or snapshot task references under the locks before printing. No debugger command or task transition was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#sad-task-list-read-lock-recheck-ek9374).

<a id="ek9375"></a>
### EK9375 — SAD's `RA` and `RC` loops wrap at the largest accepted byte count.

The debugger parses the requested byte count with `GetL()`, which accumulates up to eight hexadecimal digits into 32-bit `ULONG` (`rom/exec/debug_internal.c:461-478`). Both `RA` and `RC` use `for (t = 1; t <= cnt; t++)` with an `ULONG` counter (`:361-391`). For the accepted value `FFFFFFFF`, after processing `ULONG_MAX`, the defined unsigned increment wraps `t` to zero and the loop condition remains true.

**Trigger and consequence:** an operator issues `RA` or `RC` with count `FFFFFFFF` and the supplied address range remains readable throughout the loop. The counter then wraps and the debugger does not complete the requested read. If the range becomes unreadable first, the command may fault instead; the source does not establish that a full 4 GiB readable range is ordinarily available. **Affected configuration:** builds that include the generic SAD debugger command. **Confidence:** high for parsing the maximum and unsigned counter wrap; practical nontermination depends on the memory range remaining readable. Use a zero-based bounded loop or reject counts that cannot be safely traversed. No debugger command or memory read was performed; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#sad-read-loop-unsigned-wrap-recheck-ek9375).

<a id="ek9376"></a>
### EK9376 — The m68k `ChangeDecoration` thunk passes guest-layout storage to native Intuition.

The generated Intuition vector-912 thunk translates the m68k A0 pointer with `THUNK_PTR()` and passes it directly to native `ChangeDecoration()`; it performs no `NewDecorator` shadow or field conversion (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:6041-6047`; `m68kemu_thunks.h:34-38`). For an unshadowed pointer, the translator returns the host mapping of the guest memory (`m68kemu_intern.h:114-125`). The public structure contains a `Node` plus pointer- and `IPTR`-sized fields (`compiler/include/intuition/intuition.h:885-900`), so its 32-bit m68k layout differs from the 64-bit native layout used by supported emulator hosts. Native `ChangeDecoration()` reads and writes those fields and enqueues the structure's embedded node (`rom/intuition/changedecorationa.c:63-108`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an emulated m68k client invokes the private AROS-specific `ChangeDecoration()` vector with a guest-allocated `NewDecorator` on a 64-bit native host. Native Intuition interprets guest fields at host offsets; the class/tag/offset values can be misread and the offset writes can extend beyond the guest object. This can corrupt guest memory or Intuition state. **Affected configuration:** m68k emulation on supported 64-bit native hosts, when an emulated client calls this private AROS-only vector. The maintained Decoration utility is a native client, and no maintained m68k guest caller was found, so practical reachability remains external/conditional. **Confidence:** high for the absent structure conversion and layout mismatch; exact writes depend on the supplied guest object and native path. Add a dedicated `NewDecorator` shadow/conversion or reject this vector for guest callers. No emulator or vector call was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#m68k-changedecoration-guest-structure-layout-recheck-ek9376).

<a id="ek9377"></a>
### EK9377 — The m68k screen-notification thunk returns an untranslated native handle.

The generated `StartScreenNotifyTagList` thunk translates the input tag list to native form and frees that temporary list, but returns the native `APTR` unchanged (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:6050-6056`). Native Intuition allocates and registers an `IntScreenNotify` object with `AllocVec()` and returns its pointer (`rom/intuition/startscreennotifytaglist.c:73-78,113-121`). The matching generated `EndScreenNotify` thunk treats its A0 argument as a guest address and translates it with `THUNK_PTR()` before calling native Intuition (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:6059-6064`). A native allocation is not an address in the guest's memory mapping, and the returned native address may also be truncated to the m68k pointer width.

**Trigger and consequence:** an emulated m68k client successfully starts a screen notification and then uses the returned handle with `EndScreenNotify()`. The handle does not identify the native notification when translated back, so it cannot reliably deregister the entry; the notification can remain registered and retain its resources. The API describes the return as private and says clients should only test it against zero, but `EndScreenNotify()` explicitly accepts the handle returned by `StartScreenNotifyTagList()`, so this limits normal lifecycle use. **Affected configuration:** m68k emulation on supported native hosts when a guest calls these Intuition vectors; no maintained guest caller was found. **Confidence:** high for the asymmetry between native-pointer return and guest-pointer argument translation; exact failure depends on pointer values and host width. Return a guest-visible handle token with a native mapping and translate it back in `EndScreenNotify()`. No emulator or notification operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#m68k-screen-notification-handle-roundtrip-recheck-ek9377).

<a id="ek9378"></a>
### EK9378 — Android Exec selects unavailable context APIs and retains a freed HostLib interface after init failure.

The Android-specific Exec options state that `swapcontext()` and its companions are unimplemented on ARM Linux and missing on Android, but still define `HAVE_SWAPCONTEXT` and add `newstackswap` to the selected objects (`arch/all-linux/android/exec/make.opts:2-6`). That macro adds `getcontext`, `makecontext` and `swapcontext` to the HostLib symbol request and to `LibCInterface` (`arch/all-unix/exec/platform_init.c:12-21`; `exec_platform.h:50-57`). HostLib documents that unresolved entries remain NULL in the allocated interface (`arch/all-hosted/hostlib/getinterface.c:25-49`). When any are unresolved, `Platform_Init()` drops the interface and closes the library, but leaves `PD(SysBase).SysIFace` pointing to the freed array (`platform_init.c:40-51`). The INITLIB dispatcher reports the failure, but `Exec_Init()` ignores `set_call_libfuncs()`'s return (`rom/exec/exec_init.c:277-280`; `compiler/libinit/libinit.c:24-50`). The selected `NewStackSwap()` later dereferences the interface for `getcontext`, `makecontext` and `swapcontext` (`arch/all-unix/exec/newstackswap.c:68-106`); DOS `RunCommand()` is a selected caller (`rom/dos/runcommand.c:127-166`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an Android target uses this option set and HostLib cannot resolve one or more context functions, as the checked-in Android option comment anticipates. Exec continues after `Platform_Init()` fails. A later stack-swapped command reaches `NewStackSwap()` through a pointer to the dropped interface; it may read freed interface memory or dispatch through a NULL/invalid function entry, preventing command execution and potentially faulting the task. **Affected configuration:** the Android Linux Exec variant selecting `arch/all-linux/android/exec/make.opts`; other Unix variants are not implicated by this option-specific failure. **Confidence:** high for the contradictory feature selection, incomplete-interface cleanup, stale published pointer and ignored initialization result; the exact failure at call time depends on allocator reuse and unresolved entries. Do not select `newstackswap` unless the host APIs are available; also clear the interface pointer and fail/abort platform initialization when required symbols are missing. No Android build, HostLib resolution, or stack swap was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#android-stack-swap-hostlib-failure-recheck-ek9378).

<a id="ek9379"></a>
### EK9379 — `CONDSTATE_METRIC` calls a conducted player's optional hook without checking for NULL.

`CreatePlayerA()` documents `PLAYER_Hook` as optional and defaulting to none, while `PLAYER_Conducted` is a separate flag that defaults to FALSE (`workbench/libs/realtime/createplayera.c:43-55,89-92`). `SetPlayerAttrsA()` stores the hook and toggles the conducted flag in independent tag cases without requiring a hook when the flag is set (`setplayerattrsa.c:251-261`). For `CONDSTATE_METRIC`, `SetConductorState()` selects the first `PLAYERF_CONDUCTED` entry and passes `pl_Hook` directly to `CallHookA()` without a NULL check (`setconductorstate.c:175-201`). `CallHookA()` dispatches `hook->h_Entry` (`compiler/alib/callhook.c:48-50`; `compiler/include/utility/hooks.h:82-90`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a caller creates or updates a player with `PLAYER_Conducted=TRUE` but no `PLAYER_Hook`, then requests `SetConductorState(..., CONDSTATE_METRIC, ...)` for its conductor. The metric path selects that player and dereferences the NULL hook while dispatching, faulting the caller instead of reporting that no metric handler is available. **Affected configuration:** realtime.library clients using the public conducted-player and `CONDSTATE_METRIC` APIs. No checked-in caller requests `CONDSTATE_METRIC`; the triggering sequence is presently external/future-client dependent. **Confidence:** high for the independent public tag semantics and unchecked dispatch; no local caller establishes current in-tree reachability. Require a non-NULL hook before selecting the maestro or return a defined error when none is available. No player or metric request was created; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#realtime-condstate-metric-null-hook-recheck-ek9379).

<a id="ek9380"></a>
### EK9380 — `SystemTagList()` dereferences a failed `ExtArg` allocation after creating a shell process.

After `CreateNewProc()` succeeds, `SystemTagList()` allocates an `ExtArg` with `AllocMem()` and immediately writes `ea->ea_CES` without checking for NULL (`rom/dos/systemtaglist.c:402-414`). The function does not send the startup packet until later (`:443-474`), so the dereference occurs while the newly created child has not received the packet that initializes its CLI. The subsequent cleanup of the packet object and cloned tag list is also bypassed by the fault (`:489-502`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a `SystemTagList()` launch reaches successful `CreateNewProc()`, then the `ExtArg` allocation fails. The caller dereferences NULL and faults instead of returning a launch error; the child has already been created but has not received its startup packet, and the normal packet/tag cleanup is skipped. The child’s eventual state depends on the process startup path; no stronger claim is made. **Affected configuration:** DOS builds using this `SystemTagList()` path for shell/CLI launches. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation, immediate write and ordering before `SendPkt`; occurrence requires the stated allocation failure. Check the allocation before initializing or publishing the extension, and unwind the child and owned launch resources on failure. No allocation failure, shell launch or child process was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5691).

<a id="ek9381"></a>
### EK9381 — `SystemTagList()` copies a command into an unchecked allocation when it needs a trailing newline.

For a nonempty command that does not end in a newline, `SystemTagList()` allocates `commandlen + 2` bytes for a terminated copy but does not check the result before copying and appending the newline (`rom/dos/systemtaglist.c:257-268`). The unchecked destination reaches `CopyMem()` and the subsequent indexed writes before the function can report failure. The selected hosted emergency-console caller passes an empty command, so it does not exercise this branch; this is a public DOS API failure path.

**Trigger and consequence:** a caller passes a nonempty command lacking a final newline and `AllocVec(commandlen + 2, ...)` fails. `SystemTagList()` writes through NULL while constructing the injected command instead of returning an error, faulting the caller and bypassing its normal cleanup. **Affected configuration:** DOS builds using `SystemTagList()` with the stated command and allocation failure; no checked-in caller with proven matching input was found in the reviewed paths. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation and writes; occurrence requires memory exhaustion at that allocation. Check `cmdcopy` before copying and follow the existing `end` cleanup path on failure. No allocation failure or command launch was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5692).

<a id="ek9382"></a>
### EK9382 — `SystemTagList()` silently starts a command without the caller's current directory when `DupLock()` fails.

When the caller does not supply `NP_CurrentDir`, `SystemTagList()` attempts to duplicate the caller's current directory, but does not check whether `DupLock()` failed (`rom/dos/systemtaglist.c:394-400,448-461`). It places the resulting `BNULL` into the startup packet and proceeds to send it. `NewCliProc` installs that value with `CurrentDir(newdir)` (`rom/dos/newcliproc.c:142-165`). For a later relative-path open, DOS uses the process current directory when present, but falls back to the boot process's directory when it is NULL (`rom/dos/open.c:191-205`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a `SystemTagList()` caller relies on inheriting its current directory, has a non-null current-directory lock, and `DupLock()` fails. The child still launches, but relative paths resolve from the boot process's directory instead of the caller's; file operations can silently target the wrong location or fail. **Affected configuration:** DOS builds using `SystemTagList()` without an explicit `NP_CurrentDir`, when the caller has a current directory and duplication fails. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked result and NULL-to-boot-directory fallback; occurrence requires the stated lock duplication failure. Treat a failed duplication as launch failure, or explicitly preserve the documented inheritance behavior. No lock failure, shell launch or file operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5693).

<a id="ek9383"></a>
### EK9383 — `CliInitNewcli()` dereferences a NULL startup packet despite documenting NULL as a supported input.

`CliInitNewcli()` documents that a NULL startup packet uses defaults, but its vector wrapper forwards `dp` unchanged to `internal_CliInitAny()` (`rom/dos/cliinitnewcli.c:24-35,48-51`). The helper reads `dp->dp_Type` and logs other packet fields before any null handling (`rom/dos/newcliproc.c:57-82`), so a direct NULL call dereferences address zero. The selected `AROS_CLI` startup macro handles a NULL packet itself by waiting for and retrieving the startup message before calling `CliInitNewcli()` (`compiler/include/dos/cliinit.h:145-156`); that standard path does not pass NULL to the vector. The optional m68kemu bridge does translate guest address zero to native NULL for this vector (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks.c:1084-1087`), although no guest caller using that form was established.

**Trigger and consequence:** a direct `CliInitNewcli(NULL)` call, including a guest call through the optional m68kemu bridge, reaches the helper and faults while reading the packet instead of using defaults. **Affected configuration:** DOS clients that call the public vector with NULL; the selected `AROS_CLI` macro path is excluded, and emulator reachability depends on guest behavior. **Confidence:** high for the documented contract and unconditional dereference; no maintained native caller passing NULL was found. Implement the documented default path before reading packet fields or revise the API contract and callers consistently. No call or guest execution was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L788).

<a id="ek9385"></a>
### EK9385 — Deeply nested `Disable()` calls can re-enable interrupts before their matching `Enable()` calls.

`IDNestCnt` is a signed `BYTE` (`compiler/include/exec/execbase.inc:57`), and newly created tasks start it at -1 (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:235`). `Disable()` increments the counter; the selected PC SMP backend performs an explicit byte atomic increment, and the Amiga m68k vector uses `addq.b` (`rom/exec/disable.c:83-89`; `arch/all-pc/exec/exec_platform.h:137-147`; `arch/m68k-amiga/exec/disable.S:69-73`). After 130 nested calls on one task/CPU, byte wrap changes the count from -1 to -127. The first corresponding `Enable()` decrements it to -128; generic `Enable()` treats any negative count as permission to call `KrnSti()` (`rom/exec/enable.c:85-99`), and the Amiga vector likewise enables when its signed-byte decrement is negative (`arch/m68k-amiga/exec/enable.S:70-75`). Thus interrupts are re-enabled with 129 Disable levels still outstanding.

**Trigger and consequence:** a call chain nests 130 `Disable()` operations on the same task/CPU and then begins unwinding with `Enable()`. On byte-wrapping implementations, the first Enable can turn interrupts on before the remaining critical sections have ended, allowing interrupt handlers to observe or modify their protected state. **Affected configuration:** selected m68k-Amiga and PC backends with byte-sized counter operations; other targets store the count in `BYTE` too, but compiler-specific signed narrowing behavior is not claimed here without an explicit byte-operation check. No checked-in 130-deep caller was found, so this is a conditional public API boundary. **Confidence:** high for the arithmetic and early-enable branch on the named backends; occurrence requires extreme nesting and subsequent Enable. Widen the counter or detect overflow rather than allowing wrap. No nested call, interrupt or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5819).

<a id="ek8827"></a>
### EK8827 — Forbid nesting can wrap into the switch-enabled range on m68k-Amiga.

`tc_TDNestCnt` is a signed `BYTE` initialized to -1 for new tasks (`compiler/include/exec/tasks.h:39`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:236`). The selected m68k-Amiga `Forbid()` vector increments it with `addq.b` (`arch/m68k-amiga/exec/forbid.S:63-67`). After 130 nested calls the byte wraps to -127; the first `Permit()` decrements it to -128 (`rom/exec/permit.c:85-93`). Since `Permit()` schedules when the resulting task-disable count and interrupt-disable count are both negative and a switch is pending, this wrap can admit a task switch while 129 Forbid levels remain outstanding. This is specifically an m68k-Amiga signed-byte path; the generic C counter behavior on other targets is not included without a selected byte-operation check.

**Trigger and consequence:** an m68k-Amiga call chain nests 130 `Forbid()` calls on one task, then calls `Permit()` while a reschedule is pending and interrupts are enabled. The scheduler can switch tasks before the remaining critical sections unwind, allowing another task to access state the caller still assumes protected. **Affected configuration:** m68k-Amiga builds selecting the byte-increment assembly vector and generic `Permit()`; no checked-in 130-deep caller was found. **Confidence:** high for signed-byte wrap and the negative-count scheduling gate; occurrence requires extreme nesting plus a pending switch. Widen the nesting state or detect overflow before the count wraps. No nested call, schedule or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ek8827-forbid-nesting-overflow-recheck).

<a id="ek9386"></a>
### EK9386 — InstallAROS continues file-copy setup after its shared I/O buffer allocation fails.

`InstallStage__OM_NEW()` sizes a shared file-copy buffer from `AvailMem()`, enforces a 511-byte minimum and 64 MiB maximum, then stores `AllocMem()`'s result without checking it (`workbench/tools/InstallAROS/ia_stageclass.c:163-194`). It continues initialization and returns the stage object (`:195-389`). Later, the undo path passes the buffer to `BackUpFile()` (`:1897-1907`), whose read/write loop uses the supplied pointer without a NULL check (`workbench/tools/InstallAROS/ia_diskio.c:807-829`); the regular copy path likewise passes it to DOS `Read()` and `Write()` (`ia_stageclass.c:1911-1947`). Disposal merely skips `FreeMem()` when the pointer is NULL (`:392-401`), so it does not prevent use.

**Trigger and consequence:** the optional InstallAROS tool is built and its stage object is constructed, but the shared buffer allocation fails; the user then proceeds to copy or back up a file. The installer submits a NULL buffer to the file I/O path instead of rejecting the stage or reporting allocation failure. The resulting error or fault depends on the selected filesystem/handler's handling of a NULL data pointer; no universal crash is claimed. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-tools-installaros` builds; the parent `workbench-tools` dependency is commented out in this revision, so default Workbench inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation and subsequent NULL-capable call chain; practical outcome depends on the handler and the allocation-failure trigger. Abort stage construction or reject file operations when the shared buffer is unavailable. No allocation failure, installer operation, filesystem I/O or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5894).

<a id="ek9400"></a>
### EK9400 — PC SMP startup failures leave discovered CPUs counted and eligible for task affinity (conditional unschedulable CPU affinity; high source confidence).

The all-PC ACPI parser builds `apic_count` from discovered processors before SMP startup (`arch/all-pc/kernel/acpi_apic.c:252-260`). `smp_Initialize()` resets it to one only when `smp_Setup()` fails (`arch/all-pc/kernel/smp.c:362-370`). Later startup failures do not reconcile that count: `smp_Wake()` returns early if an AP stack allocation fails (`:261-264`); it continues after a wake error or readiness timeout (`:280-314`); and `smp_Entry()` releases the readiness lock even when `cpu_InitBootStrap()` returns NULL, then halts instead of joining the scheduler (`:118-147`). The platform-post caller only prints the count when initialization succeeds and otherwise proceeds without correcting it (`arch/all-pc/kernel/platform_post.c:201-205`). `KrnGetCPUCount()` exposes the stale count, processor.resource snapshots it into `cpucount`, and `SetTaskAffinity()` validates affinity bits against that count (`arch/all-pc/kernel/getcpucount.c:12-24`; `rom/processor/init.c:17-48`; `rom/task/SetTaskAffinity.c:82-109`). The PC scheduler filters ready tasks by the selected CPU's affinity mask (`arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:117-121`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an all-PC SMP system discovers multiple APs, but one or more fail during stack allocation, wakeup, readiness, or bootstrap-task creation. The published CPU count still includes those APs, so callers can successfully set a task's affinity exclusively to an offline CPU ID. No online scheduler matches that mask, leaving the task ready but unscheduled. **Affected configuration:** i386-PC or x86-64-PC SMP with multiple discovered processors and a later AP-startup failure; non-SMP and `smp_Setup()` failure (which resets the count) are excluded. **Confidence:** high for the stale count and accepted affinity range; the task stall requires a caller to select an offline CPU exclusively. Reconcile online CPU membership/count after each AP outcome and validate affinity against online CPUs. No AP, allocation failure, affinity change, schedule or build was exercised; source-only; see the [PC SMP AP-count failure trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ek9400-ap-count-reconciliation).

<a id="ek9401"></a>
### EK9401 — A failed CPU-mask allocation makes an x86-64 processor probe report CPU 0's data for another CPU (conditional processor information misattribution; high source confidence).

`Processor_Init()` creates one high-priority query task per discovered CPU. It allocates a CPU mask and passes it through `KrnGetCPUMask()` as that task's affinity (`arch/all-pc/processor/processor_init.c:100-138`). `KrnAllocCPUMask()` returns NULL when its allocation fails (`arch/all-pc/kernel/alloccpumask.c:15-37`); `KrnGetCPUMask()` forwards the pointer, and the APIC helper explicitly tolerates NULL without populating a mask (`arch/all-pc/kernel/getcpumask.c:13-20`; `arch/all-pc/kernel/apic.c:115-134`). The selected x86-64 `PrepareContext()` replaces the task's inherited mask with the supplied pointer, including NULL (`arch/x86_64-all/exec/preparecontext.c:37-51`). In the PC scheduler, a NULL affinity mask admits the task on CPU 0 and excludes it on other CPUs (`arch/all-pc/kernel/apic.c:137-149`; `kernel_scheduler.c:117-121`).

The query task's `PQData` retains the requested CPU number and that CPU's destination record. `Processor_QueryTask()` calls `ReadProcessorInformation()` into that record and updates topology using the requested CPU number (`processor_init.c:27-55`). The information reader executes CPUID on the CPU where the task runs (`processor_util.c:607-619`; CPUID instruction wrappers in `processor_arch_intern.h:53-57`).
