For a source of length `L < n`, the first loop writes its NUL at index `L` but does not advance the pointer or decrement `n`; the remaining count is already `n-L` after the `L` non-NUL bytes. The padding loop writes exactly `n-L` bytes at indices `L` through `n-1`. For a source of length at least `n`, the first loop writes at most indices `0` through `n-1`; for `n == 0`, neither loop writes. Therefore the implementation does not write beyond the `n`-byte bound, and the original `n+1` count double-counted the NUL at index `L`. No string operation was run; source-only.

<a id="ek10759"></a>
### EK10759 — WITHDRAWN: signed-byte arguments to stdc `tolower()` are guarded

This candidate is withdrawn after checking the selected AROS ctype implementation. The inline `tolower()` body tests `(unsigned)c <= 255` before indexing and otherwise returns `c` unchanged (`compiler/crt/stdc/include/aros/stdc/ctype.h:60-61`); its out-of-line implementation has the same guard (`compiler/crt/stdc/ctype.c:81-85`). Thus the signed-byte arguments in `strcasecmp()`, `strncasecmp()`, and `strcasestr()` do not index before the table in this implementation. The configured byte tables map ASCII letters and leave bytes 0x80-0xff unchanged (`compiler/crt/stdc/__ctype.c:270-345`), so no selected-locale comparison defect was established. No runtime call was made. Source-only.

<a id="ek10760"></a>
### EK10760 — stdc `strcasestr()` reads past both strings for an empty search string

`strcasestr()` sets `len_s` to `strlen(search)` but has no empty-search special case (`compiler/crt/stdc/strcasestr.c:46-91`). When `search` is empty, the first-character comparison succeeds on the two NUL bytes and `done` is zero. The comparison loop then evaluates `--done`; because `done` is unsigned, it wraps to `SIZE_MAX` and is true. The loop reads `search[1]` and `str[1]`, both beyond their terminating NULs, and can continue reading beyond either object until a comparison differs. The companion `strstr()` explicitly returns the haystack when the needle is empty.

**Trigger and consequence:** call `strcasestr(haystack, ""). The implementation performs out-of-bounds reads beyond the empty search string and beyond the haystack terminator; the resulting behavior is undefined and can also return an invalid pointer. **Affected configuration:** all builds using this stdc `strcasestr()` implementation. **Confidence:** high from the unsigned decrement and subsequent dereferences; no search was run. Return `haystack` immediately when the search length is zero. Source-only. See the [stdc substring-search review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-substring-search-review-ek10759-ek10760).

<a id="ek10761"></a>
### EK10761 — stdc `arc4random()` fallback does not satisfy its cryptographic-strength contract

The stdc `arc4random()` and `arc4random_buf()` documentation promises cryptographically strong output suitable for keys, nonces, and tokens (`compiler/crt/stdc/arc4random.c:22-39`; `arc4random_buf.c:23-29`; `arc4random_uniform.c:22-36`). When `entropy.resource` is unavailable or `OpenResource()` fails, `__arc4random_buf()` silently fills the output with `arc4_fallback()` (`__arc4random.c:55-79`). That fallback is a 32-bit xorshift-style generator whose state is initialized from second-resolution `time(NULL)`, stack and base/task addresses, and a per-base incrementing counter (`__arc4random.c:28-49`). These inputs and this generator do not provide the documented cryptographic-strength guarantee.

**Trigger and consequence:** use any of the three selected stdc `arc4random` vectors in a configuration where `entropy.resource` is absent or unavailable. The call still succeeds, but its output is only the fallback sequence and is not suitable for the security-sensitive uses promised by the public documentation. **Affected configuration:** stdc builds and runtime setups where `OpenResource("entropy.resource")` returns NULL, or where entropy calls fail and fallback supplies the remaining bytes; the compiler target's entropy dependency is optional (`compiler/crt/stdc/mmakefile.src:766`). **Confidence:** high that the fallback path is non-cryptographic and contradicts the API documentation; no random output was generated or assessed. Either ensure a cryptographic generator is available before exporting this guarantee, or explicitly report/document degraded output so callers do not mistake it for cryptographic randomness. Source-only; the separate resource-present but software-only entropy condition is tracked as OD11446 in the Other Drivers report.

<a id="ek10762"></a>
### EK10762 — `AddEntropy()`'s accumulated estimate has no reporting API [low impact, high confidence; optional entropy.resource]

`AddEntropy()` accepts a caller-supplied bit estimate and updates `EntropyBase->eb_Bits` under the resource lock (`rom/entropy/addentropy.c:41-44,70-80`). Its function documentation says this counter is reported by `GetEntropyInfo()`. But `GetEntropyInfo()` returns only `eb_Flags` and documents those source-quality flags (`rom/entropy/getentropyinfo.c:25-39,60`); the public header likewise defines `EIF_*` source flags only (`compiler/include/resources/entropy.h:15-32`), and the resource vector list exposes no separate estimate accessor (`rom/entropy/entropy.conf:15-19`). A repository-wide reference search found no other read of `eb_Bits`.

**Trigger and consequence:** any caller supplies nonzero `bits` to `AddEntropy()`. The estimate is accumulated internally but callers cannot retrieve it through the published API, contrary to the `AddEntropy()` documentation; the value currently has no observable use. **Affected configuration:** the entropy resource module is individually buildable, but its aggregate `kernel-entropy` dependency is commented in the checked-in root and architecture build edges, so this is not claimed for the default package targets. **Confidence:** high that the documented reporting path is absent in this snapshot; whether the tally is intended to be public or the `AddEntropy()` documentation is stale needs maintainer intent. Either expose a separate estimate query or remove the unsupported reporting claim and unused counter. Source-only; no resource or caller was run.


<a id="ek10763"></a>
### EK10763 — stdc `strrev()` forms a pointer before the string for empty input

`strrev()` advances `end` to the terminating NUL and then unconditionally decrements it (`compiler/crt/stdc/strrev.c:48-53`). For an empty string, `end` initially points at the first byte of the object, so `end--` forms a pointer before that object; this is undefined pointer arithmetic. The subsequent relational comparison with `start` does not make the pointer formation valid.

**Trigger and consequence:** call the selected `strrev()` extension with a valid empty writable string. The implementation has undefined behavior before it can return the original pointer; behavior may vary by compiler and target. This has a checked-in route: FKey accepts an `INSERT ` tooltype with an empty suffix (`workbench/tools/commodities/FKey.c:1546-1549`), copies that empty parameter into zero-initialized `KeyInfo`, then `RethinkKey()` passes it to `strrev()` (`:839-847`). Its GUI also allows selecting Insert Text while the string gadget is empty; the cycle notification reaches `CmdToKey()` and `RethinkAction()` (`:740-744,810,887-911`). **Affected configuration:** the stdc implementation on any target when called with empty input; the in-tree FKey route is the explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-commodities` target, whose parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/commodities/mmakefile.src:20-23`). **Confidence:** high for the unconditional decrement and both empty-parameter paths; no GUI or function call was run. Return early when the string is empty, or use an end-exclusive pointer. Source-only.

<a id="ek10764"></a>
### EK10764 — WITHDRAWN: `strxfrm()` inherits no `strncpy()` overrun

This derivative candidate is withdrawn with EK10758. `strxfrm()` delegates to `strncpy(dst, src, n)` (`compiler/crt/stdc/strxfrm.c:54-57`), and the selected copy writes no byte beyond index `n-1`; `strxfrm()`'s documented maximum of `n` output bytes is therefore respected by this path. `strxfrm_l()` delegates to the same implementation (`compiler/crt/posixc/strxfrm_l.c:9-12`). No string operation was run; source-only.


<a id="ek10765"></a>
### EK10765 — stdc `strtod()` overflows its signed exponent accumulator

`strtod()` accumulates every exponent digit in an `int` with `exp = exp * 10 + digit` and applies the result using `pow(10, exp)` (`compiler/crt/stdc/strtod.c:150-166`). It never checks the accumulator against `INT_MAX` before multiplication/addition.

**Trigger and consequence:** on an FPU-enabled build, pass a valid decimal with an exponent magnitude greater than `INT_MAX`, such as `1e2147483648`. The signed `int` accumulation overflows, which is undefined behavior; the parsed magnitude and returned value can be wrong. This also occurs for a sufficiently long exponent digit sequence. **Affected configuration:** builds using the selected floating-point `strtod()` implementation; `strtof()`, `strtold()`, and `atof()` delegate to it (`compiler/crt/stdc/strtof.c:54`; `strtold.c:59`; `atof.c:43`). Builds with `AROS_NOFPU` compile the separate stub instead. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked signed arithmetic; no conversion was run. Bound the exponent accumulation and handle values outside the representable result range without overflowing the accumulator. Source-only.


<a id="ek10766"></a>
### EK10766 — unsigned string conversions negate the overflow sentinel

`strtoul()` and `strtoull()` set their result to `ULONG_MAX`/`ULLONG_MAX` when the parsed magnitude overflows, then unconditionally negate that saturated result when the input had a minus sign (`compiler/crt/stdc/strtoul.c:166-183`; `strtoull.c:166-182`). Unsigned negation wraps, so an overflowing negative subject sequence returns a small value (for example, the negation of the maximum is 1). POSIX says an out-of-range correct value returns the unsigned maximum; an Austin Group/WG14 clarification request notes that inherited C wording is ambiguous here but describes magnitude-first overflow handling as the intended interpretation. `strtoumax()` delegates to one of these functions and inherits the behavior (`strtoumax.c:52-59`).

**Trigger and consequence:** call one of these functions on a negative decimal whose magnitude exceeds the destination unsigned type's maximum, such as `-18446744073709551616` for 64-bit `unsigned long long`. The conversion sets `errno` to `ERANGE` but returns 1 rather than `ULLONG_MAX`; callers that inspect the returned value can accept or propagate an incorrect small value. **Affected configuration:** builds using these selected unsigned converters, with the exact threshold depending on the width of the return type; `strtoumax()` is affected through delegation. **Confidence:** high for the source behavior; medium for the standards interpretation because the WG14 clarification request documents ambiguity in the inherited wording. No conversion was run. Preserve the overflow sentinel when the magnitude has already overflowed, subject to the intended contract. Source-only.


<a id="ek10767"></a>
### EK10767 — stdc `strtod()` does not parse hexadecimal floating constants

The selected `strtod()` scans decimal digits, a decimal point, and a decimal `e` exponent, then returns; it has no branch for a `0x`/`0X` hexadecimal significand or `p`/`P` binary exponent (`compiler/crt/stdc/strtod.c:118-167`). Its own documentation labels it a C99 function. C99's required subject-sequence forms include hexadecimal floating-point values ([WG14 N1256, §7.20.1.3](https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg14/www/docs/n1256.pdf)).

**Trigger and consequence:** convert a valid hexadecimal floating string such as `0x1p2`. The routine consumes only the initial `0`, returns 0, and leaves `endptr` at `x`, instead of returning 4 and consuming the full value. **Affected configuration:** FPU-enabled builds using this stdc implementation; `strtof()`, `strtold()`, and `atof()` use the same parser. **Confidence:** high from the complete parser path and its documented C99 API; no conversion was run. Add hexadecimal significand and binary-exponent parsing. Source-only.

<a id="ek10768"></a>
### EK10768 — ExecSMP scheduler kicks can use a task-owned affinity mask after task termination

In ExecSMP builds, `SetTaskPri()` takes the target task spinlock, observes `TS_RUN` on another CPU, and saves `IntETask(...)->iet_CpuAffinity` in `remoteCpuAffinity` (`rom/exec/settaskpri.c:73-83,115-126`). It then drops the task/list locks before calling `KrnScheduleCPU(remoteCpuAffinity)` (`:136-148`). The lock protects the read, but not the later use of this pointer. `SetTaskAffinity()` has the same gap: it updates or installs the target mask under the task lock, releases it, then calls `KrnScheduleCPU(cur)` when a running task must be kicked (`rom/task/SetTaskAffinity.c:111-142`). `Signal()` also caches the target mask, releases the task lock, and later calls `KrnScheduleCPU()` for remote running or newly readied tasks (`rom/exec/signal.c:323-336,365-377,430-438`). In the wait-to-ready path, its own comment warns that another core may run and free the target after it becomes ready, but the cached mask remains task-owned.

A concurrently terminating target can pass through `RemTask()` into `CleanupETask()`, which frees a non-sentinel affinity mask (`rom/exec/remtask.c:111-132`; `rom/exec/exec_util.c:238-260`). If cleanup runs after one of these paths releases its task lock and before `KrnScheduleCPU()` consumes the saved pointer, the scheduler receives freed storage. The all-PC `KrnScheduleCPU()` path copies the mask in `core_DoIPI()`; ARM32 and AArch64 native paths directly dereference the mask to form the IPI target bits (`arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_ipi.c:177-179`; `arch/arm-native/kernel/schedulecpu.c:20-41`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/schedulecpu.c:20-39`). `SetTaskAffinity()` documents that allocated masks are freed with the task (`rom/task/SetTaskAffinity.c:98-100`); task removal ends that lifetime.

**Trigger and consequence:** on an ExecSMP target with CPU affinity enabled, call `SetTaskPri()` or `SetTaskAffinity()` for a remotely running task, or `Signal()` a remotely running/waiting task whose affinity excludes the caller CPU, while target termination wins the interval between task-lock release and `KrnScheduleCPU()` consuming the finite mask. In `Signal()`'s wait-to-ready branch, the task may also run and terminate immediately after the ready-state publication and before the scheduler call. The scheduler can copy/read freed memory, potentially sending an incorrect reschedule IPI or faulting. `TASKAFFINITY_ANY` is a sentinel and is excluded from this specific pointer-read trigger. **Affected configuration:** ExecSMP all-PC and ARM-native SMP targets, including configured x86-64 PC and Raspberry Pi SMP builds; requires finite per-task affinity and concurrent task removal. **Confidence:** high that the mask lifetime is not held across the call; race occurrence and exact effect depend on scheduling. No priority/affinity change, signal, removal race, IPI, or build was run. Source-only. See the [scheduler affinity-mask lifetime trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#settaskpri-remote-affinity-mask-ek10768).

<a id="ek10769"></a>
### EK10769 — Efika idle paths spin instead of executing their power-save instruction [conditional]

The selected Efika `idleTask()` contains its supervisor/interrupt-enabled `MSR_POW` sequence only inside `if (0)`, so the runnable idle task loops without a sleep or yield (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/kernel_init.c:516-545`). `Kernel_Init()` installs this function as a priority -128 task (`:652-696`). The separate empty-ready-list path in the selected Efika scheduler also loops with interrupts enabled but leaves its `MSR_POW` instruction commented out (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/scheduler.c:86-105`); dispatch explicitly clears `MSR_POW` from the selected context before return (`:155-159`). Thus neither idle path enters the source's documented power-save state.

**Trigger and consequence:** an explicitly built Efika system has no higher-priority runnable work and executes the idle task, or enters the scheduler's empty-ready-list wait. The CPU continues executing a polling loop rather than entering the power-save state indicated by the dormant code. This defeats the intended idle power reduction; the actual power and thermal effect depends on hardware and was not measured. **Affected configuration:** the explicit CHRP Efika kernel target (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/kernel/mmakefile.src:6-23`); the parent Efika image dependency is commented in its boot manifest (`arch/ppc-chrp/efika/boot/mmakefile.src:5-16`), so default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high that the selected paths never execute `MSR_POW`; medium for the practical power impact. Enable a supported wait/power instruction in both idle paths, or revise the documented behavior if active spinning is intentional. No Efika hardware, scheduler, power state or build was exercised; source-only; see the [Efika idle power-path trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#efika-idle-power-path-ek10769).
<a id="ek10770"></a>
### EK10770 — DOSBoot device rows can exceed their fixed label buffer [conditional]

For each device row, `populateGadgets_PageBoot()` allocates `sizeof(struct Node) + 96` bytes and points `ln_Name` immediately after the node (`rom/dosboot/menu.c:312-318`). The valid-media formatting path then writes an unbounded `NewRawDoFmt()` string into that 96-byte region, including the device-node name and `fssm_Device` name with `%s` conversions (`:371-380`). Exec's `RAWFMTFUNC_STRING` implementation writes each output byte and the final NUL through an incrementing pointer without a capacity argument (`rom/exec/rawdofmt.c:123-131,400-410`). The DOS structures define both names as BSTRs with a representable maximum length of 255 bytes and impose no shorter bound in this row path (`compiler/include/dos/bptr.h:57-68,75-83`; `compiler/include/dos/filehandler.h:87-94,102-120`).

**Trigger and consequence:** enter DOSBoot's optional Boot Options page with media present and a row whose formatted name and fields exceed 96 bytes. For example, two 30-character names already produce at least 101 bytes including the terminator with small numeric fields. `NewRawDoFmt()` writes beyond the allocated row label into adjacent memory; this can corrupt heap data or cause later menu setup/use to fail. **Affected configuration:** DOSBoot builds with the optional Boot Options page enabled; requires a MountList device row with sufficiently long names and the valid-media formatting branch. **Confidence:** high for the fixed 96-byte destination and unbounded formatter; medium for reaching the required name lengths through a configured device node. Size the label from the actual formatted length or use a bounded formatter and handle truncation. No long-name row, menu, or build was exercised; source-only; see the [DOSBoot device-row formatting trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-device-row-format-capacity-ek10770).

**Coverage:** [DOSBoot device-row formatting trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-device-row-format-capacity-ek10770).

<a id="ek10771"></a>
### EK10771 — `stpsym()` writes past a zero- or one-byte destination and fails to consume truncated symbols

The selected SAS/C compatibility implementation writes the first alphabetic character before checking `dest_size`, then writes a terminating NUL at `dest_ptr[count]` (`compiler/crt/stdc/stpsym.c:68-81`). For `dest_size` 0 or 1, a valid symbol therefore writes two bytes despite the supplied capacity. For a positive undersized buffer, the copy loop stops when the destination is full but returns the pointer at that truncation point, although the documented result is the pointer after the symbol (`:34-38,73-81`). A caller that continues scanning from the returned pointer can treat the remaining alphanumeric suffix as another token. The header exposes this API (`compiler/crt/stdc/include/aros/stdc/string.h:110`); no direct in-tree callsite was found beyond its own example, so the parser consequence is conditional on an external caller.

**Trigger and consequence:** call `stpsym()` with an alphabetic input and a destination capacity of 0 or 1, causing a two-byte write into a smaller destination; or call it with a positive capacity smaller than the symbol and continue from its returned pointer, causing one symbol to be split into a copied prefix and remaining suffix. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the stdc implementation; requires caller-provided capacity/input combination. **Confidence:** high for the write and return behavior against the function's documented contract; external caller impact is conditional. Check capacity before writing, and scan to the symbol end even when output truncates. No call or build was run; source-only; see the [SAS/C helper review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#sas-c-string-helper-review-ek10771).


<a id="ek840"></a>
### EK840 — Selected DOS commands use a borrowed CLI process after its list lock is released [conditional; ExecSMP]

`FindCliProc()` takes `rn_RootLock` while searching the CLI list, stores the matching `Process *`, releases the semaphore, and returns the unpinned pointer (`rom/dos/findcliproc.c:52-68`). Selected `Break PROCESS` and `ChangeTaskPri PROCESS` use local `Forbid()` around lookup and operation (`workbench/c/Break.c:139-144`; `workbench/c/ChangeTaskPri.c:86-104`). `Status PROCESS` instead obtains `rn_RootLock`, performs a temporary local `Forbid()` around `FindCliProc()`, then ends Forbid and releases the root lock before calling `printProcess()` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Status.c:150-172`). That print routine immediately dereferences `process->pr_CLI` and reads process and CLI fields (`:199-224`). Exec documents that Forbid on ExecSMP blocks scheduling only on the calling processor and does not protect shared data from another CPU (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-66`). A CLI process can therefore exit on another CPU after lookup: `DosEntry()` removes its CLI entry before returning (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:978-985`), then self-removing `RemTask()` queues the retired task for cleanup by the service task (`rom/exec/remtask.c:130-141,165-181`; `rom/exec/service.c:73-89`). The `Process` allocation is part of the task's `tc_MemEntry` (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:411-421`). `Break` can then call `Signal()` on the retired task; `ChangeTaskPri` can pass it to `SetTaskPri()`, which reads task fields and its lock. `Status` can race the same exit and cleanup while formatting the borrowed pointer and CLI data.

**Trigger and consequence:** on ExecSMP, use `Break PROCESS <number>`, `ChangeTaskPri PROCESS <number>`, or `Status PROCESS <number>` while the target CLI exits on another CPU after `FindCliProc()` returns. Break and ChangeTaskPri can dereference a retired Process/Task pointer; Status can dereference the retired process and CLI while printing; the outcome depends on whether cleanup has freed or reused the memory. **Affected configuration:** selected `workbench-c` commands on ExecSMP; requires a concurrent exit of the named CLI. `Status PROCESS` shares the conditional ExecSMP lifetime gap: after releasing the root lock, it reads the borrowed process and CLI during formatting, while another CPU can remove the CLI and complete task cleanup. **Confidence:** high for the borrowed-pointer and cross-CPU lifetime gap; exact visible failure depends on timing and memory reuse. The lookup and operation need a shared lifetime mechanism, or the API must return a stable reference. No command, process exit race, or build was run; source-only; see the [FindCliProc caller-lifetime review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#findcliproc-borrowed-process-lifetime-ek840).


<a id="ek10772"></a>
### EK10772 — `Resident REMOVE` leaves task switching forbidden after finding a segment

`Resident` calls `Forbid()` before searching for the requested segment (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Resident.c:119-122`). The missing-segment branch balances it with `Permit()`, but when a segment is found none of the exits does: successful `RemSegment()` falls through to `RETURN_OK`, the internal-command branch changes `seg_UC` to `CMD_DISABLED` and returns success, and the in-use branch reports an error and returns warning without permitting. `RemSegment()` itself edits the resident list and frees the segment but does not call `Permit()` (`rom/dos/remsegment.c:58-94`). Exec stores the forbid nesting count with the task across `Wait()` and restores it when that task resumes (`rom/exec/wait.c:80-90,121-126`), so a later wait does not clear the leaked forbid.

**Trigger and consequence:** run `Resident NAME REMOVE` when `NAME` resolves to a segment in either resident list. The command returns with one extra forbid nesting level in the calling task. Subsequent code on that task can continue without task switching until it explicitly balances the count; blocking in `Wait()` only temporarily allows other tasks to run and restores the leaked count after wakeup. On ExecSMP, this affects the calling CPU's dispatch state, not all CPUs. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the `Resident` command; requires an existing matching segment. **Confidence:** high for the unmatched `Forbid()` on every found-segment path and Exec's save/restore semantics; practical scheduling impact depends on the caller's subsequent behavior. Balance the forbid on every found path before returning or calling other DOS routines. No resident command, task scheduling or build was run; source-only; see the [Resident command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#resident-command-full-body-forbid-balance-ek10772).


<a id="ek10773"></a>
### EK10773 — `Run` silently drops `+` continuation text when its join buffer allocation fails [conditional]

When input remains buffered after `ReadArgs()`, `Run` computes the continuation length and allocates a buffer to join it to the parsed command (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Run.c:98-121`). If `AllocMem()` fails, the failure branch only sets `cmdsize = 0`; it leaves `command` pointing at the original parsed command and continues to launch it through `SystemTagList()` (`:119-159`). It neither reports the allocation failure nor consumes/joins the buffered continuation. The normal error cleanup is not taken because launch can succeed.

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke `Run` with a `+`-continued command and enough buffered continuation text for `argsize > 0`, then fail the join-buffer allocation. `Run` starts a background process with only the first parsed command text, while the continuation remains in the parent shell's input stream. The requested command and arguments are therefore split or incomplete. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the `Run` shell command; requires continuation input and allocation failure. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked fallback and successful launch path; exact parent-shell handling of the remaining text depends on shell state. Return an allocation error before launching or preserve the continuation as part of an explicit retry path. No command, allocation failure or build was run; source-only; see the [Run command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#run-command-full-body-continuation-allocation-ek10773).


<a id="ek10774"></a>
### EK10774 — `Execute` copies long script names past the CLI command-name buffer [conditional]

DOS allocates `cli_CommandName` as a BSTR with a 255-byte payload by default (`rom/dos/allocdosobject.c:81-91,119-121`). The selected Shell accepts input lines up to 512 bytes (`workbench/c/Shell/state.h:12`; `readLine.c:79-119`). After opening the script, `Execute` takes the full `SHArg(NAME)` length, stores it in the one-byte BSTR length, then copies all `len` bytes to the 255-byte payload without checking the bound (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Execute.c:207-211`). The checked `SetProgramName()` helper rejects names longer than 255 bytes, but this command writes the CLI field directly (`rom/dos/setprogramname.c:75-91`).

**Trigger and consequence:** run `Execute` with an existing script path longer than 255 bytes that fits in the shell input line. `Execute` writes past the allocated `cli_CommandName` BSTR into adjacent memory; the one-byte stored length also truncates/wraps. **Affected configuration:** builds using the selected `Execute` shell command and default DOS CLI allocation; requires a long, successfully opened script path. **Confidence:** high for the 255-byte allocation, unchecked copy, and larger accepted line length; filesystem/path availability is environment-dependent. Reject names over 255 bytes or use a dynamically sized CLI command-name field. No long path, script, or build was used; source-only; see the [Execute command full-body review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#execute-command-full-body-name-boundary-ek10774).


<a id="ek10775"></a>
### EK10775 — `Execute` reports argument-buffer failure after switching the shell to the script [conditional]

`Execute` first changes `cli_CurrentInput` to the requested script or to a temporary file containing the script and remaining shell input, and updates `cli_CommandName` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Execute.c:113-205`). When command arguments are present, it then calls `SetVBuf()` to install the argument line in `cli_StandardInput`. If that allocation fails, the command returns `RETURN_FAIL` immediately without restoring the prior CLI input/name or freeing `extraargs` (`:213-229`). The selected Shell resumes its loop using `cli_CurrentInput` (`workbench/c/Shell/readLine.c:54`; `Shell.c:88-110,255-264`), so it proceeds to read the script even though `Execute` reported failure.

**Trigger and consequence:** run `Execute script arguments` after the script input handoff succeeds, then fail `SetVBuf()`'s buffer allocation. `Execute` reports failure, but leaves the script installed as the shell's current input, so subsequent shell processing can execute it without the requested injected arguments; if the continuation buffer was allocated, that buffer is also leaked on this return. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting `Execute`; requires nonempty arguments and a `SetVBuf()` allocation failure. **Confidence:** high for state-change ordering, the direct error return, and the Shell's subsequent use of `cli_CurrentInput`; script execution depends on the later shell loop continuing. Roll back the CLI state and release temporary buffers before returning, or make the command handoff atomic. No script or allocation failure was run; source-only; see the [Execute argument-buffer failure caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#execute-setvbuf-failure-state-retention-ek10775).


<a id="ek10776"></a>
### EK10776 — `Execute` silently omits buffered continuation arguments when its join allocation fails [conditional]

When text remains buffered after `ReadArgs()`, `Execute` allocates `extraargs` to join the parsed `ARGUMENTS` with that unread text (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Execute.c:82-98`). If `AllocVec()` fails, the code simply skips the join and continues; `arguments` still refers only to the explicitly parsed text (or the empty string). The later script path can still be installed and executed, with only that incomplete argument value injected (`:113-121,213-227`). No allocation error is reported.

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke `Execute` with buffered continuation text and fail the `extraargs` allocation. The requested script runs without the continuation portion of its command arguments; the parent input remains positioned at that text, so it is not part of the script's injected argument line. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the `Execute` shell command; requires unread buffered input after `ReadArgs()` and allocation failure. **Confidence:** high for the skipped join, retained `arguments` pointer and continuing script path; later interpretation of leftover parent input depends on shell state. Treat the failed allocation as command failure or preserve the continuation explicitly. No allocation failure, script or build was run; source-only; see the [Execute continuation allocation trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#execute-continuation-join-allocation-ek10776).


<a id="ek10777"></a>
### EK10777 — `Pipe` launches a pipeline stage with `NIL:` input after handle duplication fails [conditional]

For each left-hand pipeline stage, `pcharExecute()` creates its input using the unchecked expression `OpenFromLock(DupLockFromFH(in))` and passes the result as `SYS_Input` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Pipe.c:129-145`). `OpenFromLock()` returns `BNULL` on a failed conversion and leaves the supplied lock to be freed by its caller (`rom/dos/openfromlock.c:43-55,64-94`). `SystemTagList()` interprets a `SYS_Input` value of `BNULL` by opening `NIL:` (`rom/dos/systemtaglist.c:145-156,215-219`), so the left stage can still launch successfully without the input stream it was supposed to receive. The Pipe helper neither checks `cis` nor retains/frees the intermediate lock if conversion fails.

**Trigger and consequence:** run a pipeline with a left-hand stage while `DupLockFromFH(in)` or `OpenFromLock()` fails. The stage is launched with null-device input instead of the caller's input; when lock duplication succeeded but `OpenFromLock()` failed, the duplicated lock is also leaked. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the `Pipe` shell command; requires a pipeline and a DOS handler/handle duplication or allocation failure. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked call, `BNULL` fallback and OpenFromLock ownership contract; occurrence depends on the stated failure. Abort the pipeline and free any intermediate lock/handle when duplication fails. No pipe, process launch or failure was exercised; source-only; see the [Pipe command full-body review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#pipe-command-full-body-input-ownership-ek10777).


<a id="ek10778"></a>
### EK10778 — `CD` retries lock-name allocation indefinitely after low-memory failure [conditional]

`GetLockName()` increases an unsigned `ULONG` allocation size by 256 until either `NameFromLock()` succeeds or `error` becomes nonzero (`workbench/c/shellcommands/CD.c:115-141`). On an `AllocVec()` failure it assigns `error = IoErr()` and retries if that value is zero. The selected Exec `AllocVec()` wrapper returns NULL on allocation failure without setting DOS `IoErr()` (`rom/exec/allocvec.c:54-67`), so a zero or stale-zero error leaves the retry condition true. The increment eventually wraps `i`, and the function continues retrying instead of returning. `CD` calls this helper both after changing the current directory and when printing the current directory (`CD.c:72-99`).

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke `CD` on a path whose first `GetLockName()` allocation fails while `IoErr()` is zero. The command remains in the retry loop, repeatedly attempting allocations as the unsigned size grows and wraps, so it does not return normally and can consume CPU under memory pressure. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the `CD` shell command; requires initial 256-byte allocation failure and zero `IoErr()`. **Confidence:** high for the loop condition, unsigned wrap, and `AllocVec()` error behavior; occurrence depends on the stated low-memory/error state. Return immediately on allocation failure rather than using DOS `IoErr()` to decide whether to retry. No allocation failure, directory operation or build was run; source-only; see the [CD command full-body review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cd-command-full-body-getlockname-retry-ek10778).


<a id="ek10779"></a>
### EK10779 — `Path RESET` frees the next list node before using it [conditional]

`Path RESET` saves `cur->next` in `next`, then frees `BADDR(cur->next)` rather than `cur` before assigning `cur = next` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Path.c:104-121`). For a list with at least two entries this frees the node that the next loop iteration treats as current; that iteration reads its fields and may free its successor again. The original head is never freed.

**Trigger and consequence:** run `Path RESET` with two or more command-path entries. The loop traverses freed `PathEntry` storage and can corrupt the heap or fault; it also leaks the old head. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the `Path` shell command; requires a path list of at least two entries. **Confidence:** high for the incorrect freed pointer and next-iteration use. Free `cur` after saving its successor.

No path operation or build was run; source-only; see the [Path command full-body review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#path-command-full-body-list-lifetime-ek10779).


<a id="ek10780"></a>
### EK10780 — `Path` can pass a NULL FileInfoBlock to `Examine()` after allocation failure [conditional]

`IsDirectory()` allocates a `DOS_FIB` and immediately calls `Examine(lock, fib)` without checking whether the allocation succeeded (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Path.c:339-350`). The selected `Examine()` implementation forwards the FIB to the filesystem and, when the operation succeeds, unconditionally calls `fixfib(fib)` and reads `fib->fib_FileName` (`rom/dos/examine.c:62-66`). A successful examine with a NULL FIB therefore dereferences NULL.

**Trigger and consequence:** add a path whose `Lock()` succeeds while `AllocDosObject(DOS_FIB)` fails, and the filesystem accepts the examine packet. The DOS wrapper dereferences the missing FIB and faults instead of rejecting the path. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the `Path` shell command and selected DOS implementation; requires FIB allocation failure. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked argument and selected Examine success-path dereference; the handler's response to the malformed packet depends on the filesystem. Check the allocation before calling `Examine()`.

No path operation or build was run; source-only; see the [Path command full-body review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#path-command-full-body-list-lifetime-ek10779).


<a id="ek10781"></a>
### EK10781 — `Path ADD` dereferences a NULL insertion predecessor after an earlier path fails [conditional]

The `ADD` loop assigns `insertAfter = InsertPathEntry(...)` for each new name without preserving the prior valid predecessor when insertion fails (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Path.c:163-188`). `InsertPathEntry()` returns NULL when allocation, locking, or directory validation fails (`:293-333`). If a later name is otherwise valid, the next call reaches `predecessor->next` with that NULL predecessor (`:305-310`).

**Trigger and consequence:** add at least two new path names in one `Path` invocation; the first insertion fails, then a later name locks and validates as a directory. The later insertion dereferences NULL and faults rather than reporting/continuing safely. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the `Path` shell command; requires an insertion failure followed by another eligible name. **Confidence:** high for the returned-NULL assignment and unchecked dereference. Retain the list-head/successful predecessor when an insertion fails, and stop or continue with a checked predecessor.

No path operation or build was run; source-only; see the [Path command full-body review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#path-command-full-body-list-lifetime-ek10779).


<a id="ek10782"></a>
### EK10782 — `Path` leaks its FileInfoBlock when `Examine()` fails [conditional]

`IsDirectory()` frees its allocated `DOS_FIB` only inside the successful `Examine()` branch (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Path.c:344-388`). If the filesystem rejects the examine request or returns an I/O error, the helper returns FALSE without `FreeDosObject(DOS_FIB, fib)`. Each such failed path check leaks one FIB allocation.

**Trigger and consequence:** `Path ADD` obtains a lock and FIB for a candidate path, then `Examine()` fails. The command rejects the path but retains the DOS_FIB allocation, consuming memory on repeated failures. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting `Path`; requires an examine failure after successful FIB allocation. **Confidence:** high for the allocation and branch-specific missing release. Move `FreeDosObject()` to common cleanup.

No path operation or build was run; source-only; see the [Path command full-body review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#path-command-full-body-list-lifetime-ek10779).


<a id="ek10783"></a>
### EK10783 — `Setenv` and `Unsetenv` report success when their `ENV:` listings fail [conditional]

In listing mode, after `Lock("ENV:")` succeeds, both `Setenv` and `Unsetenv` silently skip output if `AllocDosObject(DOS_FIB)` fails and ignore a false result from `Examine()` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Setenv.c:121-143`; `Unsetenv.c:110-132`). Their `while (ExNext(...))` loops treat every false return as normal end-of-directory without checking `IoErr()`, although the DOS `ExNext()` contract requires distinguishing `ERROR_NO_MORE_ENTRIES` from a real error (`rom/dos/exnext.c:35-51`). Both commands then return `RETURN_OK` (`Setenv.c:157-159`; `Unsetenv.c:145-147`).

**Trigger and consequence:** run `Setenv` or `Unsetenv` with no arguments when `ENV:` opens but FIB allocation, initial examination, or a later directory read fails. The command prints no failure and returns success, presenting an absent or partial environment-variable list as complete. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting either command; requires listing mode and one of the stated allocation/filesystem failures. **Confidence:** high for each unchecked result and the success return; practical impact depends on the failure. Report allocation/examination failures and check `IoErr()` after enumeration ends. No environment listing or failure was run; source-only; see the [Setenv command full-body error-path review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#setenv-command-full-body-listing-errors-ek10783).


<a id="ek10784"></a>
### EK10784 — `Get` and `Getenv` silently truncate variable values longer than 255 bytes [conditional]

`Getenv` reads global variables into a fixed 256-byte buffer and prints any successful `GetVar()` result as complete (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Getenv.c:62-74`). `Get` does the same for local variables (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Get.c:58-72`). The selected `GetVar()` implementations copy at most the requested size and insert a NUL terminator at the boundary; the local path reports the stored variable length through `IoErr()`, and the global path records the file size there (`rom/dos/getvar.c:115-164,241-275`). The selected `Setenv` and `Set` commands pass their full values to `SetVar()` without a 255-byte limit (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Setenv.c:91-102`; `Set.c:77-93`), and the shell accepts command lines up to 512 bytes (`workbench/c/Shell/state.h:12`).

**Trigger and consequence:** store a global value longer than 255 bytes with `Setenv` and query it with `Getenv`, or create a local value with `Set` and query it with `Get`. Each getter prints only the first 255 bytes and returns success without a truncation indication. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the corresponding setter/getter pair; requires a long value without an earlier newline. **Confidence:** high for both fixed destinations, GetVar truncation, and successful print; long values can be created by the selected setters. Allocate based on the stored size or detect and report truncation. No environment variable was created or queried; source-only; see the [Getenv full-body and Setenv producer pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#getenv-command-full-body-value-bound-ek10784).


<a id="ek10785"></a>
### EK10785 — `If ... VAL` treats invalid numeric operands as zero [conditional]

In numeric comparison mode, `doeval()` declares `val1` and `val2`, calls `StrToLong()` for both operands, ignores both return values, then compares the outputs (`workbench/c/shellcommands/If.c:251-273`). The selected `StrToLong()` writes zero and returns -1 when it cannot parse a number; it also accepts a numeric prefix without requiring the entire operand to be consumed (`rom/dos/strtolong.c:59-77`). Thus invalid or partially numeric text can be treated as a valid number.

**Trigger and consequence:** use a numeric condition such as `If invalid EQ 0 VAL` or `If 12x EQ 12 VAL` in a script. The condition evaluates TRUE even though an operand is not a complete valid integer, so the wrong branch executes. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the `If` command; requires `VAL` comparison with malformed operands. **Confidence:** high for the ignored parser results and demonstrated return/output semantics. Require successful full-string conversion before comparing. No script or comparison was run; source-only; see the [If command full-body evaluation pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#if-command-full-body-evaluation-and-error-status-ek10785).

<a id="ek10786"></a>
### EK10786 — `If` returns success after reporting script-context or block-matching errors [conditional]

When invoked outside a script, `If` prints `ERROR_SCRIPT_ONLY`; when a false condition reaches EOF without a matching `Else` or `EndIf`, it prints `ERROR_NO_MATCHING_ELSEENDIF` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/If.c:228-240`). Both paths then fall through to an unconditional `RETURN_OK`. The selected Shell copies each command's result into `cli_Result2` and the script failure-level handling relies on that status (`workbench/c/Shell/Shell.c:255-280,514-582`).

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke `If` in an interactive shell, or evaluate a false condition in a malformed script block with no matching terminator. The command prints an error but reports success, so callers and `FailAt` processing cannot distinguish the failure from a valid If. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting `If`; requires either invalid context or an unmatched false block. **Confidence:** high for both diagnostics and the shared success return. Return an error status on these diagnosed failures. No command or script was run; source-only; see the [If command full-body evaluation pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#if-command-full-body-evaluation-and-error-status-ek10785).


<a id="ek10787"></a>
### EK10787 — `Skip` reports success when a label-less skip has no `EndSkip` [conditional]

`Skip` documents that omitting `LABEL` searches for the first `EndSkip`, and that failure to find the target returns an error (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Skip.c:18-34`). At EOF, the scan exits with `labelFound == FALSE`; however, the final failure check only runs when `SHArg(LABEL) != NULL` (`:85-95`). A label-less skip therefore returns `RETURN_OK` even though no `EndSkip` was found.

**Trigger and consequence:** execute `Skip` without a label in a script that reaches EOF before an `EndSkip`. The command reports success instead of the documented missing-target error; `FailAt` and shell callers cannot detect the malformed skip block. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the `Skip` command; requires a label-less skip with no later EndSkip. **Confidence:** high for the documented behavior, EOF loop exit and conditional error guard. Treat EOF without the requested EndSkip as failure. No script or command was run; source-only; see the [shell control-flow commands pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#shell-control-flow-command-full-body-pass-ek10787).


<a id="ek10788"></a>
### EK10788 — `Ask` treats the suffix of an overlong response as a second answer [conditional]

`Ask` reads each response with `FGets(..., 100)`, accepts only a small fixed set of answers, then immediately prompts and reads again when the returned text is unrecognized (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Ask.c:63-111`). The selected DOS `FGets()` stops after 99 bytes without draining the rest of the physical line (`rom/dos/fgets.c:48-75`). Therefore the next prompt consumes the leftover suffix of the same input line as a new response.

**Trigger and consequence:** enter an overlong response whose first 99 bytes are invalid and whose remaining suffix is `yes` (or `y`). The command accepts that suffix on the next iteration and returns `RETURN_WARN`, as if the user answered yes to a separate prompt. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting `Ask`; requires an input line longer than 99 bytes with a yes token in the unread suffix. **Confidence:** high for the fixed read bound, retained unread input, retry loop and accepted yes tokens. Drain the remainder of any overlong line and reject that response as a whole. No prompt or input was run; source-only; see the [Ask command full-body input pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ask-command-full-body-input-boundary-ek10788).


<a id="ek10789"></a>
### EK10789 — `Cut` moves its bounds-parser pointer before the input on an invalid start [conditional]

`getBoundaries()` advances `buffer` by the return value of `StrToLong()` without checking for conversion failure (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Cut.c:213-229`). The selected `StrToLong()` returns -1 when the operand does not start with a digit and writes zero to the output (`rom/dos/strtolong.c:59-64`). For an invalid start token such as `CHAR xyz`, the pointer therefore moves one byte before the token, and the following `*buffer` test reads outside the operand before the command can reject it. The parser also ignores the conversion result for the end bound, so malformed endpoints may be accepted as an open-ended range.

**Trigger and consequence:** call the selected `Cut` command with a nonnumeric first bound, such as `Cut text CHAR xyz` or `Cut text WORD xyz`. `getBoundaries()` dereferences a pointer before the argument string; the result is undefined and can fault or produce an incorrect range. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the `Cut` shell command; requires a malformed range string. **Confidence:** high for the -1 conversion result, pointer arithmetic, and subsequent dereference; exact effect depends on adjacent memory. Reject conversion failures and require complete consumption of each bound before using it. No command or malformed input was run; source-only; see the [Cut command full-body bounds pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cut-command-full-body-bounds-pass-ek10789).


<a id="ek10790"></a>
### EK10790 — `PathPart DIR` passes an unterminated allocation to `PathPart()` [conditional]

For the `DIR` option, the command allocates exactly `strlen(DIR)` bytes and copies that many bytes, but never reserves or writes a NUL terminator before calling DOS `PathPart()` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/PathPart.c:68-75`). The selected `PathPart()` implementation scans `path` until it encounters NUL (`rom/dos/pathpart.c:60-82`). The scan therefore continues past the requested allocation boundary and may inspect allocator padding or adjacent memory before the command writes its separator position.

**Trigger and consequence:** call the selected `PathPart DIR <nonempty path>` branch. `PathPart()` reads beyond the `AllocVec(size)` object while searching for its terminator; the resulting path position depends on unrelated memory contents and can produce an invalid read or incorrect output. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the `PathPart` shell command; requires the `DIR` option and a nonempty value. **Confidence:** high for the exact allocation/copy length and NUL-terminated scan contract; whether the physical overread crosses the rounded allocator block depends on the allocated size and adjacent contents. Allocate `size + 1` and explicitly terminate the copy. No command or path was run; source-only; see the [PathPart/Fault command body pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#pathpart-and-fault-command-full-body-pass-ek10790).


<a id="ek10791"></a>
### EK10791 — `Clip GET WAIT` blocks after `StartNotify()` fails [conditional]

`Clip` initializes a notify request and calls `StartNotify()` but ignores its Boolean result before waiting on the notification signal or Ctrl-C (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Clip.c:101-127`). The selected DOS API returns FALSE when it cannot resolve/register the requested notification (`rom/dos/startnotify.c:67-69,180-202`). On that path no notification is registered to send the allocated signal, but `Clip` still enters `Wait()`.

**Trigger and consequence:** use `Clip GET WAIT` when StartNotify fails for the selected `CLIPS:<unit>` path, such as a notification registration/device error. The command can block indefinitely until Ctrl-C or an unrelated signal on the same mask. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting `Clip`; requires GET+WAIT and StartNotify failure. **Confidence:** high for the ignored false result and unconditional wait; occurrence depends on path/handler registration state. Check StartNotify and return its error before waiting.

No clipboard, notification, or build was exercised; source-only; see the [Clip command full-body review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#clip-command-full-body-and-notification-iff-pass-ek10791).


<a id="ek10792"></a>
### EK10792 — `Clip COUNT` wraps to zero when all 256 clipboard units are present [conditional]

`Clip COUNT` stores the number of occupied units 0 through 255 in an `UBYTE` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Clip.c:171-187`). If all 256 are counted, the final increment wraps the value to zero before it is printed.

**Trigger and consequence:** all clipboard unit paths `CLIPS:0` through `CLIPS:255` are counted as occupied. `Clip COUNT` prints zero instead of 256. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting `Clip`; requires all 256 units to be counted. **Confidence:** high for the UBYTE counter and 256-iteration range. Use a wider counter.

No clipboard, notification, or build was exercised; source-only; see the [Clip command full-body review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#clip-command-full-body-and-notification-iff-pass-ek10791).


<a id="ek10793"></a>
### EK10793 — `Clip COUNT` treats unrelated `Open()` errors as occupied units [conditional]

The count loop considers a unit present whenever `Open()` succeeds or `IoErr()` is anything other than `ERROR_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Clip.c:176-184`). Thus device-not-mounted, permission, and I/O failures are counted the same as an existing clipboard unit.

**Trigger and consequence:** while counting, an absent/unavailable `CLIPS:<unit>` lookup returns an error other than `ERROR_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`. `Clip COUNT` includes that unit in its occupied count and still returns success. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting `Clip`; requires COUNT and a non-not-found open failure. **Confidence:** high for the condition and count update; exact DOS error depends on provider state. Count only successful opens and explicitly handle the intended `ERROR_OBJECT_IN_USE` existence case.

No clipboard, notification, or build was exercised; source-only; see the [Clip command full-body review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#clip-command-full-body-and-notification-iff-pass-ek10791).


<a id="ek10794"></a>
### EK10794 — `Clip SET` reports success when IFF chunk finalization fails [conditional]

`toClip()` sets `ok = TRUE` as soon as `WriteChunkBytes()` writes the text payload, then ignores both `PopChunk()` results and `CloseIFF()` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Clip.c:216-230`). The selected IFFParse `PopChunk()` can fail while seeking back to patch an unknown chunk size, writing the size/pad byte, or flushing buffered output (`workbench/libs/iffparse/popchunk.c:77-143`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the text payload write succeeds but finalizing the CHRS/FTXT chunks fails. `toClip()` still returns TRUE, so `Clip SET` returns success although the clipboard IFF stream may be incomplete or malformed. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting `Clip`; requires a finalization/stream error after payload writing. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked error returns and success flag ordering. Propagate PopChunk/CloseIFF finalization errors.

No clipboard, notification, or build was exercised; source-only; see the [Clip command full-body review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#clip-command-full-body-and-notification-iff-pass-ek10791).


<a id="ek10795"></a>
### EK10795 — `Clip GET` can overflow its accumulation size when concatenating multiple text chunks [conditional]

For each additional CHRS chunk, `fromClip()` computes `filebuffer_size + cn->cn_Size + 1` in `ULONG` and allocates that result (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Clip.c:284-297`). It does not check the addition for overflow. If the aggregate text size exceeds the ULONG range, the allocation can be much smaller than `filebuffer_size`; the next `CopyMem(filebuffer, new_filebuffer, filebuffer_size)` then copies the old aggregate into that undersized block.

**Trigger and consequence:** a clipboard IFF contains multiple CHRS chunks whose cumulative text size overflows ULONG. The command can allocate an undersized result buffer and copy the prior aggregate past its end, corrupting adjacent memory. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting `Clip`; requires aggregate chunk data beyond ULONG_MAX and successful undersized allocation. **Confidence:** high for unchecked ULONG arithmetic and the subsequent copy size; practical availability depends on address space and clipboard backing. Check each cumulative-size addition before allocation.

No clipboard, notification, or build was exercised; source-only; see the [Clip command full-body review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#clip-command-full-body-and-notification-iff-pass-ek10791).


<a id="ek10796"></a>
### EK10796 — `Echo` underflows its string pointer for `FIRST` on an empty string [conditional]

When `FIRST` is nonzero but lies past the end of the string, `Echo` moves `b` to `l - 1` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Echo.c:103-112`). `l` is an unsigned `ULONG` computed as the string length (`:69,98-101`). For an empty string, `l - 1` wraps to the maximum ULONG, and the output loop then dereferences `*b` (`:119-127`).

**Trigger and consequence:** call `Echo` with an empty string argument and any positive `FIRST` value. The command forms an out-of-range pointer and dereferences it while deciding whether to print a character; behavior is undefined and can fault or read unrelated memory. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the `Echo` shell command; requires an empty string and positive FIRST. **Confidence:** high for the zero length, unsigned subtraction and dereference. Handle empty strings before applying the at-least-one-character fallback. No command or input was run; source-only; see the [Echo command full-body bounds pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#echo-command-full-body-bounds-pass-ek10796).

<a id="ek10797"></a>
### EK10797 — `Stack` can display a negative byte count for a valid large stack size [conditional]

`Stack` stores the current byte count in `LONG` after multiplying the CLI's stack units by `CLI_DEFAULTSTACK_UNIT` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Stack.c:64-66`). On 64-bit targets this multiplication is performed in the wider unsigned `size_t` type, but a requested size near `LONG_MAX` rounds up to 2,147,483,648 bytes and then narrows to signed 32-bit `LONG`.

**Trigger and consequence:** set a shell stack size in the top rounding interval near `LONG_MAX`, then query `Stack` without an argument. The reported byte count can become negative even though `cli_DefaultStack` stores the rounded stack size. **Affected configuration:** 64-bit targets where `LONG` is 32-bit and `IPTR`/`size_t` is 64-bit; requires a large accepted stack size. **Confidence:** high for the width conversion and narrowing. Keep the display calculation in an unsigned type wide enough for the result or reject values that cannot be represented by the output type. No command or build was run; source-only; see the [Stack command full-body pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stack-quit-and-registration-full-body-pass-ek10797).

<a id="ek10798"></a>
### EK10798 — built-in shell command registration failures are ignored [conditional]

The embedded command initializer ignores the return from `AddSegment()` for each command and for the `NewCLI` alias (`workbench/c/shellcommands/shellcommands_init.c:75-78`). `AddSegment()` reports failure when it cannot allocate the resident-list node or when a same-name entry already exists (`rom/dos/addsegment.c:63-76`). The resource initializer nevertheless returns success, so an allocation failure can leave a partially populated command set with no initialization error or retry.

**Trigger and consequence:** `AddSegment()` allocation fails for one of the names during embedded shell-command initialization. The shell command resource reports successful initialization, while that command (or the `NewCLI` alias) is absent from the resident command list. **Affected configuration:** embedded built-in shell-command resource; requires a registration allocation failure. **Confidence:** high for the ignored boolean result and partial registration. Check each insertion and handle partial registration consistently. No initialization or build was run; source-only; see the [Stack, Quit and registration full-body pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stack-quit-and-registration-full-body-pass-ek10797).

<a id="ek10799"></a>
### EK10799 — `Prompt` reports stale IoErr when `SetPrompt()` rejects an overlong name [conditional]

`SetPrompt()` returns `DOSFALSE` when the new prompt exceeds its 255-byte BSTR capacity, but that branch does not set IoErr (`rom/dos/setprompt.c:59-65`). The selected `Prompt` command then calls `PrintFault(IoErr(), "Prompt")` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Prompt.c:74-78`), so it reports an unrelated previous error or no error at all. The Shell accepts command lines up to 512 bytes (`workbench/c/Shell/state.h:12`; `readLine.c:79-120`), making this rejection reachable through the selected command.

**Trigger and consequence:** issue a `Prompt` command whose supplied value exceeds 255 bytes. The command returns an error status, but its diagnostic can identify the wrong cause or print no fault text. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the Shell `Prompt` command; requires an overlong prompt and the wrapper's failure branch. **Confidence:** high for the missing SetIoErr and unconditional IoErr lookup. Set a defined error before returning failure, or have the command report the length limit directly. No command was run; source-only; see the [Prompt command and SetPrompt contract pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#prompt-command-setprompt-ioerr-contract-ek10799).

<a id="ek10800"></a>
### EK10800 — POSIX pathname APIs can resolve an empty path to the current directory [conditional]

The stat-family wrappers reject an empty pathname only when `doupath` is true (`compiler/crt/posixc/{stat,lstat,stat64,lstat64}.c:66-85`). `chdir()` and `opendir()` have no corresponding rejection; `opendir()` even documents that its `Lock()` path is used “to allow opening” an empty string (`chdir.c:61-66`; `opendir.c:88-95`). `fstatat()` delegates the name to `stat()`/`lstat()` after optionally making `dirfd` current (`fstatat.c:69-76`). `open()` rejects an empty pathname only in Unix path mode; in native mode `__open()` locks and examines the path, then returns an existing directory as a directory descriptor for read-only access (`__fdesc.c:356-364,391-461`). `openat()` delegates relative paths to `open()` (`openat.c:83-91`). With an empty string, `__path_u2a()` returns the input unchanged in native mode and its Unix-to-AROS converter emits an empty string in Unix path mode (`__upath.c:59-65,88-104,309-423`). DOS `Lock("")` uses the current directory for a relative path, and the selected RAMFS returns the starting directory object for the empty component (`rom/dos/lock.c:180-201`; `rom/filesys/ram/filesystem.c:512-568`; `rom/filesys/ram/commands.c:879-904`).

**Trigger and consequence:** on the selected RAMFS, call `chdir("")` or `opendir("")` in either path mode; those calls can succeed on the current directory. In native path mode (`doupath == 0`), `stat()`/`lstat()` and their 64-bit variants, `fstatat("")`, and read-only `open("")`/`openat("")` can likewise operate on the current directory instead of failing with `ENOENT`. POSIXC `__open()` recognizes the directory from its lock and returns a directory descriptor without issuing RAMFS file-open (`__fdesc.c:433-461`). For `*at()` calls with a directory descriptor, the affected directory is that descriptor's directory. **Affected configuration:** selected POSIXC APIs; RAMFS or another handler that resolves an empty relative name to the current directory. The stat/open `doupath == 0` scope is intentional in these wrappers; `chdir()` and `opendir()` lack a mode-independent empty-path check. **Confidence:** high for the selected RAMFS resolution and wrapper paths. Reject empty pathnames before DOS lookup. No filesystem call or build was run; source-only; see the [POSIX empty-path caller pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posix-stat-empty-path-mode-recheck-ek10800).

<a id="ek10801"></a>
### EK10801 — POSIX pathname wrappers can leave errno unchanged for NULL paths in native mode [conditional]

`__path_u2a()` returns its input immediately when `doupath` is false, before its NULL safety check (`compiler/crt/posixc/__upath.c:57-69`). The `stat()`, `lstat()`, `stat64()`, and `lstat64()` wrappers then see the still-NULL result and return `-1` without setting errno (`stat.c:83-91`; corresponding branches in `lstat.c:66-74`, `stat64.c:83-91`, and `lstat64.c:66-74`). The same occurs in `chdir()` (`chdir.c:57-63`), `readlink()` (`readlink.c:54-60`), and `chown()` (`chown.c:62-70`): each returns its failure result or exits cleanup without assigning errno after conversion returns NULL. Thus the required error indicator can remain whatever a previous operation left there, rather than EFAULT.

**Trigger and consequence:** call one of the listed POSIX pathname functions with a NULL pathname while `doupath == 0`. The call fails, but `errno` is stale and cannot reliably identify the invalid pointer. **Affected configuration:** POSIXC callers using native AROS path mode; `__posixc_nixmain()` sets `doupath` on for its Unix-style startup route. **Confidence:** high for the early return, wrapper returns, and missing errno assignment. Validate NULL before the `doupath` fast path, or set EFAULT in each wrapper. No invalid call or build was run; source-only; see the [POSIX stat path-mode validation pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posix-stat-null-path-mode-recheck-ek10801).

<a id="ek10802"></a>
### EK10802 — `chown("")` can change the current directory owner in native path mode [conditional]

`chown()` rejects an empty string only when `doupath` is true (`compiler/crt/posixc/chown.c:58-68`). With native path mode, `__path_u2a()` returns the unchanged empty string; the function then calls DOS `SetOwner()` with it (`:69-96`). The selected RAMFS `ACTION_SET_OWNER` path resolves its name through `GetHardObject()` and, for an empty name, retains the object represented by the starting lock; `CmdSetOwner()` then writes the requested owner to that object (`rom/filesys/ram/ram_security.c:146-174`; `rom/filesys/ram/filesystem.c:512-568`).

**Trigger and consequence:** call `chown("", owner, group)` with explicit IDs while `doupath == 0` on a RAMFS volume with the security extension enabled and sufficient caller rights. Instead of failing with `ENOENT`, it can change the current directory's owner. **Affected configuration:** POSIXC native path mode plus RAMFS multi-user/security support; Unix-style `__posixc_nixmain()` mode rejects the empty path. **Confidence:** high for the path and selected RAMFS owner write; authorization and volume setup determine whether the change succeeds. Reject empty paths regardless of path conversion mode. No ownership operation or build was run; source-only; see the [chown empty-path caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-chown-empty-path-ramfs-trace-ek10802).

<a id="ek10803"></a>
### EK10803 — POSIXC `open()` and `mkstemp()` dereference NULL path arguments [conditional]

The selected `open()` wrapper forwards `pathname` directly to `__open()` (`compiler/crt/posixc/open.c:105-115`). Before calling `__path_u2a()` or checking for NULL, `__open()` reads `pathname[0]` in its Unix-path empty-string guard (`compiler/crt/posixc/__fdesc.c:356-364`). With `doupath == 1`, `open(NULL, ...)` therefore dereferences a null pointer. With `doupath == 0`, it bypasses the guard; `__path_u2a()` returns NULL unchanged and `__open()` returns `-1` without setting errno. `mkstemp()` has a separate direct path: it initializes `c` using `template + strlen(template)` before any validation (`compiler/crt/posixc/mkstemp.c:39-46`), so a NULL template is dereferenced in every path mode.

**Trigger and consequence:** pass a NULL pathname to selected POSIXC `open()` or `mkstemp()`. `open()` faults at the precheck in Unix-style mode and fails with stale errno in native mode; `mkstemp()` faults while evaluating `strlen()` in either mode. **Affected configuration:** selected POSIXC `open()` and `mkstemp()` APIs. **Confidence:** high for the pre-validation read and native-mode return path. Validate each pointer before indexing or measuring it and report EFAULT. No invalid call or build was run; source-only; see the [POSIXC open NULL-path review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-open-null-path-review-ek10803).

<a id="ek10804"></a>
### EK10804 — Unix path conversion blocks every name with the `/.attbin` prefix [conditional]

The `__path_u2a()` filter uses `strncmp(upath, "/.attbin", 8)` and returns NULL/`ENOENT` on a prefix match (`compiler/crt/posixc/__upath.c:74-82`). Its comment identifies the exact `/.attbin` compatibility path, but the comparison does not check that the next character is NUL or `/`.

**Trigger and consequence:** with Unix path handling enabled, use a valid path whose first component begins `/.attbin` but is a different name, such as `/.attbin-cache` or `/.attbinx`. Conversion rejects it as nonexistent, so POSIXC callers cannot access the otherwise valid object; callers that fail to check conversion errors retain their separate EK10632 behavior. **Affected configuration:** selected POSIXC APIs while `doupath` is enabled. **Confidence:** high for the prefix comparison and early return; impact requires such a filesystem name. Restrict the special case to the exact path or its intended subtree. No path call or build was run; source-only; see the [path-prefix filter review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posix-path-prefix-filter-review-ek10804).


<a id="ek10805"></a>
### EK10805 — withdrawn: terminal `..` conversion does not overrun its buffer

A source-order recheck of `__path_normalstuff_u2a()` disproved the claimed output expansion. For input `..`, `S_DOT2` sees NUL, sets a slash separator, and moves to `S_SLASH`; that state emits one `/`, after which the function writes NUL. The result is `/` (two bytes including NUL), while `__path_u2a()` requested `strlen("..") + 1`, or three bytes (`compiler/crt/posixc/__upath.c:93-103,387-431`). For `dir/..`, the same transitions produce `dir//`, six bytes including NUL for a seven-byte request. The state machine removes dot components or emits separators in place of consumed input; this does not establish an output longer than the input. No out-of-bounds write is retained. Source-only; no path or allocation was run.

<a id="ek10806"></a>
### EK10806 — POSIXC `realpath()` accepts a missing final path component [conditional]

After failing to `chdir()` into the full path, `__realpath()` calls `readlink()` on the final component and only handles results greater than zero. Every zero or negative result falls through to `getcwd()` and appends the component to the output (`compiler/crt/posixc/realpath.c:135-141,168-197`). The selected POSIXC `readlink()` explicitly returns `-1` and sets `errno` when DOS lookup fails; a non-link handler result is also converted to `-1`/`EINVAL` (`readlink.c:54-61,70-89`). `realpath()` therefore does not distinguish an existing ordinary file from a missing name, nor propagate other final-component lookup errors.

**Trigger and consequence:** call `realpath()` for a nonempty path whose parent directory exists but whose final component does not, such as a missing relative filename. `chdir(path)` and `readlink(final_component)` fail, but the implementation appends the name to the current directory and returns a non-NULL success result instead of `NULL`/`ENOENT`. **Affected configuration:** selected POSIXC implementation of `realpath()`; requires a path that reaches the final-component branch. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked `readlink()` error and return path. Verify final-component existence and preserve lookup errors before constructing the canonical result. No path operation or build was run; source-only; see the [realpath final-component error pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-realpath-final-component-error-ek10806).



<a id="ek10808"></a>
### EK10808 — realpath() ignores failure to restore the caller's directory [conditional]

After resolving the path, realpath() calls fchdir(fd) to restore the directory saved before traversal, but ignores its return value and returns the resolver result unchanged (compiler/crt/posixc/realpath.c:99-109). The selected fchdir() can fail: it returns -1 if descriptor lookup/type validation fails or if DupLock() cannot allocate a replacement current-directory lock (fchdir.c:59-77).

**Trigger and consequence:** let realpath() change the process directory during resolution, then have its restoration fchdir(fd) fail, for example because duplicating the saved lock fails. Even if path resolution succeeded, realpath() still returns the resolved path as success while the caller remains in the directory reached by the resolver. **Affected configuration:** selected POSIXC implementation; requires a path traversal that changes CWD and a restoration failure. **Confidence:** high that the failure is ignored and fchdir() can fail; the resulting current directory depends on how far resolution progressed. Check and propagate restoration failure, and preserve cleanup of the saved descriptor. No allocation failure or path call was induced; source-only; see the [realpath restore-error pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-realpath-restore-error-ek10808).


<a id="ek10809"></a>
### EK10809 — realpath() reports ELOOP one link before its configured recursion limit [conditional]

realpath() starts the resolver with a count of 40 (compiler/crt/posixc/realpath.c:15-16,99). The resolver rejects any call whose count is zero before examining the current path (:129-133), and subtracts one each time a positive readlink() result is followed (:168-177). Consequently, following the 40th link recurses with count zero and reports ELOOP before checking whether that link's target is an ordinary existing path. A chain of 39 links can reach its final target; a chain of 40 cannot.

**Trigger and consequence:** resolve a valid chain of exactly 40 symbolic links whose final target exists. realpath() returns ELOOP instead of resolving the path, so the implementation's 40-hop budget permits only 39 links. **Affected configuration:** selected POSIXC implementation where the filesystem supports symbolic links and the chain is exactly at the local recursion limit. **Confidence:** high for the off-by-one count; whether 40 links are intended as an allowed maximum is medium confidence. Check the terminal target before rejecting count zero, or initialize the budget to include the terminal resolution. No link chain or build was exercised; source-only; see the [realpath symlink-limit pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-realpath-symlink-limit-ek10809).




<a id="ek9239"></a>
### EK9239 — `ftell()` can report a successful position after buffered output fails [conditional]

Both stdc and POSIXC `ftell()` call DOS `Flush()` and ignore its result before querying the current position (`compiler/crt/stdc/ftell.c:55-68`; `compiler/crt/posixc/ftell.c:61-81`). Their selected DOS/DOS64 helpers can still return the underlying position after `Flush()` fails (`compiler/crt/stdc/__stdcio_dos64.c:65-72`; `compiler/crt/posixc/__dos64.c:73-88`). In POSIXC, `ftello()` and `ftello64()` use the same unchecked flush in `__ftello64()` (`compiler/crt/posixc/__ftello.c:35-43`); `fgetpos()` and `fgetpos64()` propagate the corresponding `ftell()`/`__ftello64()` result as a successful saved position (`fgetpos.c:53-62`; `fgetpos64.c:55-64`).

DOS `InternalFlush()` returns FALSE on a negative handler `Write()` and clears `FHF_WRITE`/`FHF_FLUSHING` while leaving the buffered position fields (`rom/dos/internalflush.c:40-54`). `Close()` only performs a final flush when `FHF_WRITE` remains set (`rom/dos/close.c:65-69`), so the failed buffer is not retried there. With DOS64, `GetFilePosition64()` adds the pending write count only when `FHF_WRITE` is set; otherwise it applies its read-buffer subtraction (`rom/dos64/getfileposition64.c:60-68`). The 32-bit `Seek(0, OFFSET_CURRENT)` helper also handles the now-cleared flag as a read handle. The selected RAM handler accepts a current-position query after a write error, establishing that a successful position result can follow the failed flush (`rom/filesys/ram/handler.c:188-190`; `rom/filesys/ram/commands.c:703-774`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a stdc/POSIXC stream has buffered output and the handler fails a write during `ftell()`, `ftello()`, `ftello64()`, `fgetpos()`, or `fgetpos64()`. The position routine can return a nonnegative value despite the failed write; the DOS write-mode flag is cleared, so `Close()` does not retry the pending bytes. On DOS64-enabled filesystems, the immediate result can also use the wrong read-buffer adjustment. Callers may treat the returned offset as valid and later restore or seek to the wrong position. **Affected configuration:** selected stdc/POSIXC streams using DOS filehandles; the concrete successful-query path was traced through RAMFS, while exact offsets depend on handler and buffer state. **Confidence:** high for ignored flush results, DOS state transition, and the successful RAMFS current-position path; requires a buffered write failure. Propagate flush errors and retain a recoverable write state. No I/O failure or build was induced; source-only. See the [DOS flush and file-position caller audit](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dos-ftell-failed-flush-position-ek9239).


<a id="ek10812"></a>
### EK10812 — POSIXC can retain a usergroup/posixc relative-library cycle when no StdC exit list is available [conditional resource leak]

__usergroup_available() obtains StdCBase before opening usergroup.library. If that lookup is NULL, it still opens usergroup and returns success without queueing __usergroup_release() (compiler/crt/posixc/__optionallibs.c:93-109). The code comment states that no exit list will drain for this base and that cleanup is deferred to __optionallibs_close() (:103-107). But the selected usergroup.library configuration declares rellib posixc (workbench/libs/usergroup/usergroup.conf:1-10), so opening usergroup retains a POSIXC relative-library reference. The POSIXC cleanup routine that closes PosixCUserGroupBase is registered only as a CLOSELIB hook (__optionallibs.c:142-167); generated per-task CLOSELIB hooks run only after that task's open count reaches zero (tools/genmodule/writestart.c:68-75,1477-1486). The retained usergroup dependency prevents that zero-count transition, while usergroup's own relative link keeps the corresponding PosixC base open: neither side reaches the hook that would release the other.
